author: Marina Amaral
title: TOC, TOC, TOC! Quem está batendo é o Super El Niño, eleitores
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Estou esperando pra ver o efeito do Super El Niño nas próximas eleições brasileiras, embora até o momento o tema “clima” não tenha tido destaque nos debates eleitorais. Quanto mais perto estivermos das urnas, maiores devem ser os impactos do fenômeno, intensificado pelas mudanças climáticas, na vida dos brasileiros, que no momento parecem mais preocupados com temas como segurança pública e economia.


Mas como será quando as chuvas torrenciais começarem a cair no Sul do Brasil, a seca abater o Norte, o Nordeste e o Centro-Oeste do país, e as ondas de calor extremo e falta de água tornarem a vida ainda mais difícil nas metrópoles do Sudeste? Como estará o humor do eleitor quando o preço dos alimentos subir e a fumaça dos incêndios florestais encobrir as capitais da Amazônia?


Se em 2024, sofremos com as inundações no Rio Grande do Sul, secas e incêndios florestais de proporções inéditas na Amazônia, a previsão é que os efeitos sejam ainda maiores neste ano

. De acordo com a atualização de 10 de agosto da NOAA (sigla em inglês da Administração Nacional Oceânica e Atmosférica dos Estados Unidos), o fenômeno, que já vem sendo sentido com o aquecimento do Pacífico, que já ultrapassa 1,8 grau a temperatura média (subiu 0,6 grau em menos de um mês), tem

95%

 de chance de atingir o ápice entre outubro e dezembro, superando os registros históricos dos últimos 60 anos.


A visita desse convidado indesejável pode ter o condão de despertar a população para a importância de priorizar a emergência climática e cobrar a conta nas urnas

. Segundo uma pesquisa divulgada em abril pelo Instituto Ipsos,

70%

 dos eleitores dizem que é preciso agir imediatamente para evitar impactos para as próximas gerações. Se isso ainda é insuficiente para pressionar os políticos, talvez a coisa mude quando os eventos extremos estiverem em curso como deve ocorrer nas próximas eleições. 


O impacto do Super El Niño pode ser mais imediato nas candidaturas dos governadores candidatos à reeleição.

Somente quatro estados brasileiros – Minas Gerais, Pará, Pernambuco e Piauí contam com planos robustos de adaptação climática

, segundo um

estudo

 do Instituto Clima e Sociedade (ICS) publicado em março deste ano. Outros oito estados contam com planos, mas baseados apenas no fortalecimento da defesa civil, o que é útil, mas insuficiente, segundo os pesquisadores.


Seria ótimo que, além de punir quem não fez a lição de casa, os eleitores usassem o critério ambiental para escolher deputados e senadores para que o Congresso pare de destruir as leis

, como fez com a aprovação do pacote da Destruição (Lei Geral do Licenciamento Ambiental), agora com a constitucionalidade em julgamento no STF (sobre isso leia a

coluna

 de Gustavo Faleiros desta semana) assim como a lei do Marco Temporal, que

voltou

 ao STF depois de o próprio tribunal ter se pronunciado no sentido contrário.


Sabemos que as opções não são muitas – daí o destaque dado pela imprensa especialista no tema à candidata ao Senado, Marina Silva.

Mas quem se preocupa com o clima, o ambiente e a democracia no país, tem alternativas de escolha para a Câmara Federal e Assembleias Legislativas

– a começar pelas

candidaturas

 indígenas já anunciadas para concorrer a cargos de deputado estadual e federal, além de outros candidatos com histórico confiável na área ambiental em partidos como Rede, PSOL, PCdoB e PT.


Já em relação à presidência, as opções se afunilam. Em uma conversa social, outro dia, ouvi de uma pessoa que não quer reeleger Lula, mas se considera democrata, feminista e ambientalista, o nome de Ronaldo Caiado, que anda circulando em algumas rodas “climáticas” como confirmei com outras pessoas envolvidas com o tema.


Uma surpresa e tanto para essa jornalista com mais de 40 anos de profissão, que lembra do atual governador de Goiás como fundador da UDR – União Democrática Ruralista – em 1985, inaugurando as milícias armadas no campo na redemocratização – e também da bancada ruralista, até hoje a principal articuladora de pautas contra a fiscalização e a proteção ambiental e o respeito aos direitos indígenas.


O próprio candidato continua a ostentar orgulhosamente seu compromisso com o agronegócio, responsável pela maior parte das emissões de gases de efeito estufa no país, e, para não …

author: anred
title: Trabajo en plataformas: la informalidad al palo
content:
Foto: Edgardo Gómez.


Un modelo de acumulación sustentado en plataformas digitales se ha instalado como respuesta a la crisis del capitalismo global. Es un nuevo tipo de negocios que conlleva una nueva relación capital trabajo y una mayor tasa de explotación. Todo sostenido en la informalidad. El manejo y análisis de los datos se ha vuelto un componente fundamental para la acumulación de capitales en esta etapa histórica. La interpretación más generalizada es que esta ha sido la respuesta a la onda larga depresiva que con altibajos se desenvuelve desde la década del ’70 del siglo pasado, agudizada por la crisis del 2008/09 que aún no ha sido resuelta y la pandemia del Covid19. Es lo que conocemos como capitalismo de plataformas.

 Por Eduardo Lucita, integrante del colectivo Economistas de Izquierda (EDI).


Nuevo tipo de negocios


Desde hace un tiempo se ha producido una verdadera explosión en el volumen de datos lo forzó  la creación de herramientas y métodos de recopilación y análisis en los que las nuevas tecnologías han sido decisivas.


Las redes sociales son el entramado que ha permitido la formulación y concreción de un modelo de acumulación sustentado en plataformas digitales que facilitan los flujos de datos para la interacción entre oferta (productores, proveedores) y demanda (usuarios, consumidores) por medio de internet. Se trata de un nuevo tipo de negocios que abarca tanto movilidad y mensajería (Uber), como alojamiento (Airbnb), consumo (Delivery) o recreación (Streaming).


Un tipo de negocios que ha crecido rápidamente en países de los cinco continentes con independencia de las diferentes formaciones sociales y niveles económico/culturales de cada país. También entre nosotros.


Desde el punto de vista laboral muestra “ventajas” como cierta flexibilidad en el manejo de los horarios y una rápida generación de ingresos pero al mismo tiempo es de una informalidad extrema (ausencia de derechos laborales, sin licencia por enfermedad, aguinaldo ni indemnización alguna) que lleva implícita una reconfiguración de las relaciones capital trabajo que ha incrementado sustancialmente la tasa de explotación. Según la asociación que nuclea a los conductores de plataformas (ACCAURA) “el trabajador asume el riesgo empresario, paga el mantenimiento, pone el vehículo, absorbe la caída de ingresos y, cuando aparece una rotura o un gasto imprevisto, debe endeudarse para no quedar fuera de la actividad.


C

ambios culturales


Las tecnologías de las comunicaciones han inducido un profundo cambio cultural en los comportamientos y los hábitos de consumidores y usuarios de bienes y servicios. Cada vez más prefieren recluirse en sus casas para ver películas o series antes que ir al cine; optar por un uber antes que por un taxi les da más seguridad y previsibilidad (conocer los datos del chofer, el tiempos de espera y el costo del servicio); priorizan la comodidad y rapidez de recibir los pedidos en casa, antes que salir a buscarlos.


La comida a domicilio es tal vez el caso más emblemático de estos cambios culturales, en los que el teléfono celular juega un rol principal. Ahora la comida se puede resolver sin necesidad de salidas o traslados  (restaurantes o locales de comidas) o dedicar tiempo a las compras y a la preparación (cocinar). Todo es más improvisado, rápido y eficaz.


Tal es el avance de este segmento de las plataformas que han crecido las dark kitchens (cocinas fantasma). Se trata de restaurantes virtuales, solo trabajan con entrega a domicilio o retiro en el lugar, que operan con bajos costos fijos (no hay salón, ni mesas, ni mozos, ni estacionamiento vehicular).


Puede pensarse que esto es producto de la vertiginosidad de los tiempos modernos que deja poco tiempo para las tareas domesticas que finalmente se tercerizan. Sin embargo las estadísticas disponibles muestran que el pedido de este tipo de servicios crece durante las noches en los días laborables pero también los fines de semana y los feriados. Incluso si al inicio el grueso de los pedidos se centraba en comidas rápidas y cafetería ahora están creciendo los pedidos de comida gourmet. El cambio cultural es profundo y muy abarcador.


De salida laboral

a la autoexplotación


En nuestro país el trabajo en plataformas (Uber, Cabify, Rappi, Pedidos Ya, Netflix, Prime Video, por solo citar algunos) se ha expandido rápidamente en los centros urbanos. Especialmente en movilidad y delivery. Este rápido crecimiento en 2024/25 se lo asocia a la falta de …

author: A.N.A.
title: Como seria uma sociedade de federação anarquista?
content:
24/04/2026


Como seria, na prática, uma sociedade baseada em federações anarquistas? Antes de tudo, ela provavelmente pareceria muito mais organizada do que seus críticos costumam imaginar, e muito menos caótica do que a própria ordem atual realmente é.


Sua estrutura básica partiria do princípio de que a coordenação deve surgir de baixo para cima, das pessoas onde elas realmente vivem e trabalham, em vez de ser imposta por um centro distante. Assembleias locais, conselhos de trabalhadores, sindicatos de inquilinos, cooperativas, redes de cuidado e associações voluntárias formariam a substância viva da sociedade. Esses não seriam fóruns simbólicos sem poder real, mas os espaços onde decisões seriam tomadas, recursos distribuídos, conflitos tratados e prioridades debatidas.


Níveis mais amplos de coordenação, regionais, inter-regionais e até internacionais, continuariam existindo, mas como federações dessas estruturas locais, construídas através de delegação em vez de dominação. Delegados carregariam mandatos específicos, seriam revogáveis a qualquer momento e atuariam como mensageiros e coordenadores, não como uma classe política.


Tecnicamente, uma sociedade assim dependeria de uma infraestrutura de coordenação democrática muito mais avançada e explícita do que aquela disponível aos movimentos anarquistas do século XX. Esse é um dos pontos centrais que muitas pessoas ainda não compreendem. Sistemas modernos de comunicação, bancos de dados distribuídos, verificação criptográfica, ferramentas abertas de contabilidade e registros públicos transparentes tornam muito mais plausível coordenar sociedades complexas sem uma burocracia estatal acima de todos.


Uma federação anarquista não significaria que todas as pessoas votariam diariamente sobre cada detalhe trivial, isso seria absurdo. Significaria camadas claras de tomada de decisão, onde a maioria dos assuntos seria resolvida localmente, e apenas questões genuinamente amplas seriam encaminhadas através de estruturas federativas. Uso de energia, transporte, cadeias de suprimento, planejamento ecológico, capacidade hospitalar, metas de produção e coordenação de emergências poderiam ser tornados publicamente legíveis por meio de sistemas compartilhados. O poder, ou o exercício do poder, se tornaria mais visível, não menos. O objetivo não é abolir a organização, mas abolir a organização sem controle público.


Socialmente, a vida cotidiana provavelmente pareceria mais participativa, mais recíproca e talvez mais exigente do que aquilo a que pessoas formadas sob a cidadania liberal passiva estão acostumadas. Esperar-se-ia que as pessoas participassem de forma significativa da vida comunitária, não como martírio gratuito, mas porque a sociedade deixaria de ser organizada em torno da passividade e da delegação para instâncias superiores. Muito do que hoje é mediado pela coerção do mercado ou pela compulsão burocrática passaria a ser organizado por normas de obrigação mútua, responsabilidade negociada e expectativa coletiva. O trabalho de cuidado seria reconhecido como central para a sociedade, em vez de tratado como trabalho invisível de fundo. A educação deixaria de focar na produção de mão de obra obediente para empregadores e passaria a cultivar seres humanos tecnicamente capazes, socialmente conscientes e aptos ao autogoverno. A pessoa comum precisaria de um nível mais elevado de alfabetização cívica, porque liberdade em larga escala exige competência, não apenas sentimento.


Economicamente, uma sociedade federativa anarquista provavelmente seria plural em suas formas, mas unificada por certos limites fundamentais. Recursos naturais, infraestrutura e as condições básicas da vida coletiva precisariam ser mantidos em comum ou sob forte gestão comunitária, porque permitir que se tornassem centros privados de poder apenas recriaria a dominação de classe sob outra aparência. A partir daí, a produção poderia ser organizada por cooperativas, associações municipais, federações de ofício e redes distribuídas de manufatura. A questão decisiva seria se a atividade produtiva permanece socialmente responsável. Na prática, isso significaria locais de trabalho administrados por trabalhadores e comunidades, compras transparentes, padrões abertos, sistemas interoperáveis e ferramentas de planejamento que permitam coordenação sem exigir um ministério estatal central controlando tudo de cima. Em uma sociedade tecnologicamente avançada, isso poderia se tornar muito mais dinâmico do que …

title: Comunicado de los Presos Políticos Mapuche del Módulo Comuneros de la Cárcel de Temuco.
content:
A continuación, difundimos el Comunicado de los Presos Políticos Mapuche del Módulo Comuneros de la Cárcel de Temuco respecto a la medida de dispersión aplicada a los lamgen Francisco Painevilo y Luis Tranamil hacia la Cárcel de Angol y al CCP Biobío de Concepción.


«Marri marri pu lonko, pu werken, pu machi , pu weichafe. Saludamos a todos aquellos que acompañan y abrazan la digna lucha de nuestro pueblo nación  mapuche.


Queremos a través de este comunicado, los ppm del módulo de comuneros mapuche de Temuco enviar nuestro apoyo y fortaleza a los peñi Francisco Painevilo y Luis Tranamil quienes en un contexto de arremetida represiva y represalias de acuerdo a la coyuntura política y las determinaciones del ministerio de seguridad pública, con la dirección nacional de gendarmería de chile como ente represor, se les ha aplicado por este gobierno fascista, el ser llevados a diferentes centros  de reclusión en primera instancia, lejos de sus lof y personas afines.


Además queremos enviar nuestro newen y fortaleza a las familias de los peñi que desde muchísimo tiempo también nos han apoyado en diferentes actividades culturales y de fortalecimiento espiritual dentro del contexto carcelario.


Enviamos nuestro newen y saludo fraterno al peñi Carlos Cancino que se encuentra en una compleja situación de salud en el Hospital penal de Santiago.Hacemos un llamado a acompañar a nuestros peñi y sus familias en las diferentes concentraciones y muestras de apoyo concreto, pu peñi que asumen la prisión política con firmeza ante el poder y su represión sistemática. Bien sabemos que las condiciones carcelarias en complejos penitenciario de alta seguridad  en Concepción  dejan de lado los derechos y condiciones diferenciadas como mapuche.Una realidad que golpea a varios pu PPM encerrados en dicho winka malal.


La situación en cuanto a  nuestro peñi Francisco Painevilo a variado puesto que hoy se encuentra en la Cárcel de  Angol.


Exigimos al poder judicial que considere el retorno de nuestros peñi al módulo de prisioneros político de Temuco y/o se hagan oído a las desicion  de nuestros peñi.Las facultades e interés político del gobierno para acallar al movimiento autonomista mapuche y sus diferentes expresiones de lucha se traducen en estas medidas arbitrarias. Entendemos que esta es una práctica habitual de gendarmería que levanta a presos sociales y los dispersa a diferentes canas, y que esto en su forma se asemeja  a  los acontecimientos sucedidos años antes y también involucra a los PPM,  hoy se aplica en el caso de los peñi del lof Rofue cuestión que responde al momento político de extremar las condiciones carcelaria en casos de alta connotación pública.


•No a la política de dispersión contra los PPM.


•Ante la  militarización y la  cárcel  la respuesta es la unidad en el weichan


•No a las Altas condenas racistas


•Retorno de los peñi Painevilo y Tranamil al módulo mapuche de Temuco.»


*Enviado a la radio.

Radio Kurruf

title: “Estamos en la calle para defender la soberanía científica”
content:
Trabajadoras y trabajadores científicos de todo el país se movilizaron en una Jornada Federal de Ciencia, Tecnología y Universidad bajo el lema colectivo “ponete la camiseta” por la ciencia, para expresar el apoyo a un sector estratégico para el desarrollo y la soberanía. Ante el Obelisco dialogamos con Giselle Santana del INTI, que declaró que la situación es “dramática” y denunció que las medidas del gobierno “están poniendo en riesgo la salud y la vida de la población por vaciar los organismos de ciencia y técnica que están al servicio, justamente, de cuidar la vida y la seguridad de la población”.

La jornada contó con la solidaridad de una nutrida columna de jubiladas y jubilados que llegaron desde el Congreso de la Nación marchando por Avenida de Mayo y la 9 de Julio, en una una nueva muestra del apoyo que expresan constantemente con otros sectores que están en lucha.

author: Nahuel Lag
title: Dolavon Produce: una experiencia agroecológica en el Valle Inferior de Chubut
content:
Por Mauricio Amaya


En Dolavon, las heladas marcan el calendario de quienes trabajan la tierra y cada cultivo requiere paciencia. Mientras buena parte del Valle Inferior del Río Chubut espera la llegada de la primavera, Rosa Ranguileo recorre el invernáculo donde cultiva verduras junto a su hijo. Allí, entre hileras de lechuga, espinaca, rúcula, acelga y hierbas aromáticas, sostienen un proyecto que hace apenas unos años parecía impensado: producir alimentos agroecológicos para la comunidad.


Hace tres años, una convocatoria de la Municipalidad de Dolavon cambiaba la rutina de un grupo de familias de esta localidad del departamento de Gaiman. Hasta ese momento,

Rosa Ranguileo apenas hacía plantines con su hijo en su casa y tenían una huerta en el patio; de repente pasaba a tener un campo para cultivar.

"En verano se vende mucho más porque también sembramos mucho más. Además del invernáculo, tenemos dos parcelas", cuenta Rosa, que es parte del

 proyecto Dolavon Produce

 o el Nodo Productivo, como lo llaman en este pueblo de casi 4.000 habitantes.  


“Comer sano cambió nuestra alimentación y la de la comunidad. Ese sabor de las verduras es inigualable y además sabemos que lo producimos con nuestras propias manos. Y la gente ve nuestro trabajo”, sintetiza. 

 El proyecto tomó forma en 2023 como parte del

Programa de Infraestructura para Entramados Productivos Regionales,

 articulado por el Ministerio de Obras Públicas de la Nación. El de Dolavon es uno de los 12 nodos que se proyectaron en todo el país. Un año después, con la llegada de Javier Milei a la Casa Rosada, la iniciativa se desfinanció y la responsabilidad quedó enteramente en manos del municipio, que recibió el apoyo de la Federación de Asociación Mutualistas de Chubut (FAMUCH) para sostenerlo. 


Foto: Dolavón Produce / Nodo Productivo


De recuperar la tierra a construir comunidad 


El ingeniero agrónomo Luis Ñancucheo es uno de los pilares de Dolavon Produce.

 Las dos hectáreas y media donde funciona el Nodo eran terrenos municipales degradados, que no tenían antecedentes productivos. Recuperarlas fue uno de los primeros desafíos.

"Con prácticas agronómicas relativamente simples, incorporando mucho abono y materia orgánica, logramos recuperar esos suelos y ponerlos a producir con muy buenos resultados", explica Luis. 


El objetivo inicial era sencillo en su formulación, aunque ambicioso en la práctica: que familias de la localidad pudieran

producir alimentos sanos para autoconsumo y comercializar el excedente, generando un ingreso sin que el acceso a la tierra fuera una barrera

. "Empezamos con nueve familias. A cada una se le asignó una parcela y al año siguiente ya habíamos ampliado el predio. Hoy son 32 familias las que forman parte del Nodo", precisa Luis.


También instalaron un sistema de riego por goteo para optimizar el uso del agua, una decisión clave en una región donde cada recurso debe administrarse cuidadosamente y donde el riego tradicional habría dificultado la producción. Para Ñancucheo, el mayor logro del proyecto fue más allá del trabajo sobre la tierra o de la comercialización de los productos. Las familias productores recibeb cada sábado a los vecinos para realizar venta directa de la cosecha en el Nodo y coordinan visitas y pedidos vía WhatsApp.


Foto: Dolavón Produce / Nodo Productivo


"Lo productivo en estos proyectos no suele ser un problema sino las relaciones entre las personas. Y ahí fue donde el proyecto resultó altamente exitoso." Al tiempo que sus trabajadores fueron aprendiendo y mejorando las tierras, el Nodo logró un sentido de pertenencia para las familias y empezaron a tejerse redes de apoyo en torno a la producción de alimentos. 


En ese sentido, Luis marca cómo el deterioro del poder adquisitivo durante los últimos años y la necesidad de multiplicar los medios para sostener cada economía familiar resultó un obstáculo para el desarrollo del Nodo durante el 2024 y 2025.  “Algunos de los productores debían salir a hacer una changa para completar sus ingresos y no podían atender su parcela —grafica Luis y agrega—. Pero creo que en esta crisis se fortalecieron esos lazos. El gran desafío fue acompañar a cada familia, entender qué le estaba pasando y ser solidarios."


Aunque hasta el momento ninguna de las familias productoras vive exclusivamente del trabajo en el Nodo, todas aún requieren de tener otro empleo para solventarse, la dimensión colectiva resulta fundamental y despertó interés en otros …

author: Jeny Pascacio
title: Fosas, fronteras y Palestina: las guerras contra la humanidad
content:
La segunda parte del recuento que hace Avispa Mídia del Semillero Guerra contra la humanidad. Las poblaciones y la naturaleza bajo asedio , convocado por el Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional (EZLN), aborda los crímenes contra la vida humana y la idea de “lo desechable” a través de distintas violencias contemporáneas desde el genocidio en Palestina, las desapariciones y asesinatos de personas en México, crímenes vinculadas a disputas territoriales y económicas; las condiciones que enfrentan las personas en desplazamiento forzado; y sobre los trabajadores frente a tecnologías emergentes y la precarización laboral.

La primera parte, la primera entrega, puedes leer aquí .

Durante estas sesiones el Capitán Insurgente Marcos destacó “la luz de resistencia y rebeldía de las madres buscadoras, a quienes, por mucho que las amemos, siempre les quedaremos a deber. Y que ahora nos impulsan a volver a caminar fuera de nuestras montañas, porque los brazos y los besos siempre es mejor darlos en persona y no por internet (...) y de forma especial, a las luchas, resistencias y rebeldías que han sido asediadas por siglos”.

Con la proyección de la pintura ¿Dónde estás, amor mío?, de Antonio Ramírez, basada en las madres buscadoras, la periodista y académica Alejandra Guillén habló de ‘Desaparición y leva para la acumulación de capital. Grietas de resistencia ante el nuevo dominio’.

“Es para ellas (madres buscadoras) también toda mi palabra y mucha de la que recojo viene de ellas, de sus hijos y de todas las personas que anónimamente hablan para explicar lo que está ocurriendo. Este es un saludo para las madres buscadoras que, lamentablemente, cada vez son más en este país”, dijo.

Recordó la historia de Jorge, ocurrida hace casi catorce años en Jiquilpan, en 2012, que coincide con el surgimiento del Cártel Jalisco Nueva Generación que desde sus inicios recurrió al reclutamiento forzado y al trabajo esclavo para conformar sus estructuras, una práctica que entonces aún no era reconocida como patrón de desaparición.

Las pistas reunidas por la familia, relató la periodista, ubicaban a Jorge en ranchos de la región de Tapalpa, un territorio que identificó como estratégico para la consolidación de la organización criminal y de economías legales e ilegales, como la explotación forestal y minera. En ese mismo periodo, añadió, también desaparecieron defensores del territorio en la Sierra de Manantlán, entre ellos Celedonio Monroy Prudencio, hubo el desplazamiento de comunidades enteras y el despojo sistemático de ranchos y tierras mediante las llamadas "limpias".

“Estaban sacando las maderas preciosas, las especies, las minas (...) Y lo han hecho, digamos, en alianza siempre con las mineras de la región. Y todo esto salía por los puertos, no solo en Jalisco, en toda la sierra de Jalisco y toda la sierra de Michoacán. Todo estaba ocurriendo al mismo tiempo”, precisó Alejandra Guillén.

Pero la expansión respondió a una estrategia previamente diseñada, articulada con rutas comerciales que permitían el intercambio de insumos para la producción de drogas sintéticas y otras mercancías provenientes de Asia.

La periodista hizo hincapié en que los grupos criminales en México constituyen apenas el nivel más visible de una red que involucra a actores financieros, políticos y empresariales. Entonces la violencia opera como parte de un modelo económico con objetivos de largo plazo, más que como una sucesión de hechos aislados.

En ese esquema, explicó que el reclutamiento forzado y la explotación de personas no solo sirven para conformar ejércitos, sino también para consolidar ese proyecto de expansión territorial basado en el control social y la transformación de quienes son sometidos.

En ese proceso buscan desarticular el tejido social, normalizar la crueldad e incorporar personas a un esquema de dominación que ha hecho posible ejercer un control permanente sobre barrios, pueblos y regiones.

“No es la primera vez que se esclaviza a personas, pero sí de la manera en que ha estado ocurriendo tan masivamente, decenas y decenas y decenas. Es como la fábrica del mal que instalaron, muy bien pensada, para no solo construir ejércitos, sino también transformar subjetividades (...) Y esta maquinaria ha necesitado seguir alimentándose de más personas”, lamentó Alejandra Guillén.

Recordó el caso de Teuchitlán, municipio de Jalisco, pues hizo visible el reclutamiento forzado y los circuitos de lugares donde retienen a las personas y que familias …

author: Andrea DiP
title: Quem está falando de política com a Gen Z? – com Lau Schultz
content:
O Brasil tem entre 45 e 50 milhões de jovens, pessoas com idade entre 15 e 29 anos, segundo o último levantamento do

IBGE

. Uma população diversa, majoritariamente preta ou parda e urbana. Mas como é a relação desses jovens brasileiros com a política? Como pensa uma geração tomada pela falta de perspectiva e que cresce em meio a múltiplas crises e incertezas sobre o futuro?


Para tentar entender esses cenários e paradoxos envolvendo um afastamento e tentativas de aproximação dessa

juventude com a política

, o Pauta Pública recebe a Lau Schultz, criadora de conteúdo digital e especialista em Direito do Estado. Na conversa com Andrea Dip, ela fala sobre os caminhos para disputar o imaginário político, afetos e linguagem da geração Z e destaca o papel das redes sociais nessa relação.

author: A.N.A.
title: [Espanha] A memória impressa das lutas: CNT Ciudad Real abre seu arquivo gráfico
content:
O catálogo permite buscar por título, entidade, tema ou identificador, ordenar cronologicamente as peças e consultar seu contexto


30 de julho de 2026


Um cartaz é colado para intervir no presente, não para durar. Anuncia uma manifestação, uma greve ou uma palestra, tentando condensar um ideal inteiro em uma imagem e algumas poucas palavras; depois, é arrancado, jogado no lixo ou acaba esquecido em alguma pasta.


No entanto, quando esses materiais são conservados juntos por décadas, adquirem um novo significado e começam a contar uma história mais ampla: a de como diferentes gerações nomearam seus problemas, imaginaram alternativas e se organizaram diante deles.


A 

CNT Ciudad Real

 abre agora para consulta pública o seu 

Arquivo gráfico

. Nem tudo foi produzido em Ciudad Real nem pela CNT. A coleção reúne tanto campanhas próprias da CNT Ciudad Real quanto outras provenientes de distintos territórios ou divulgadas em todo o Estado, além de materiais de outros coletivos sociais. E entre eles aparecem testemunhos especialmente valiosos da vida política e social da província, que nos oferecem um primeiro percurso pelo arquivo.


Defender o território, opor-se à guerra


Um dos exemplos mais reconhecíveis é o cartaz da manifestação realizada em Ciudad Real em 18 de setembro de 1988 contra o campo de tiro de Anchuras. Sob o lema «Anchuras também é Cabañeros», a convocatória reuniu associações, coordenadoras locais e sindicatos de numerosos municípios, entre eles a CNT. A peça recorda que as campanhas ecologistas que hoje fazem parte da memória provincial não surgiram espontaneamente nem foram concessões administrativas, mas sim se sustentaram mediante anos de mobilização popular: a Defesa 

renunciou ao projeto e colocou à venda as 4.088 hectares adquiridas para o campo de tiro

.


Dois anos depois, 

Alcázar de San Juan

 sediou três jornadas «Contra o V Centenário». Houve conferências sobre o Saara ou o conhecimento indígena, além de teatro de fantoches, desfiles de rua e um show pela solidariedade e apoio mútuo. O programa mostra uma atividade libertária provincial capaz de criar seus próprios espaços e de questionar, a partir de uma crítica ao colonialismo, o relato triunfal das celebrações de 1992.


Trabalho, cultura e memória local


A província reaparece de forma muito mais dolorosa em «Sempre colocamos os mortos», cartaz da CNT para o Primeiro de Maio de 2004. Sobre uma composição de recortes de jornal acumulam-se acidentes de trabalho, migrantes afogados, repressão e guerra. Uma das manchetes trazia o balanço ainda provisório do acidente ocorrido no complexo da Repsol em Puertollano; a explosão acabou causando 

a morte de nove trabalhadores e ferimentos em outros dezessete

. A parte inferior responde a essa geografia de mortes com um chamado direto: «É hora de mudar. Por dignidade».


Mas a memória do sindicato não se limita à denúncia. Também inclui livros, cinema, oficinas e música. O cartaz do IV Libertarock documenta o festival realizado em 2010 na antiga praça de touros de Argamasilla de Alba. No cartaz coincidiram o ska dos 

Deskaraos

, o nü metal do 

Shock

, o punk-hardcore da Pastilla Matxaka, o rock do 

Chorizo y Pan

, o punk do 

Sangre Obrera

 e o punk-rock «100% feminino» das 

Gonagón

. Os shows dividiram a programação com oficinas de língua de sinais, bumerangues e timbalada: cultura e autogestão como outra forma de encontro e organização.


Do papel às redes


As peças mais recentes permitem observar também a evolução da linguagem gráfica da CNT. As fotografias, fotocópias e composições manuais convivem agora com ilustrações digitais pensadas para circular ao mesmo tempo por paredes, centros de trabalho e redes sociais.


A campanha da greve geral feminista de 2018 apresenta mulheres diversas sob o lema 

«Paramos juntas, juntas avançamos»

. Em Ciudad Real, o comitê de greve da CNT, integrado exclusivamente por mulheres, 

avaliou a convocatória como um sucesso

 e estimou em cerca de 10 mil as pessoas que participaram da manifestação.


Cinco anos depois, o cartaz do Primeiro de Maio da 

CNT Ciudad Real

 sobrepõe fotografias e reivindicações que chamam a voltar às ruas: desemprego, acidentes de trabalho, previdência, feminismo, As Seis de La Suiza e o futuro do planeta. Sua conclusão serve também para explicar por que vale a pena conservar esses materiais: «Motivos não faltam».


Um arquivo ainda aberto


O catálogo, afirmam, permite buscar por título, entidade, tema ou …

author: Unknown
title: Political prisoner Sonay Mengütay released after 30 years
content:
Political prisoner Sonay Mengütay has been released after 30 years of imprisonment. The 52-year-old woman left Kandıra No. 1 F-Type High-Security Prison in Kocaeli, where she had been held since 2016. Outside the prison, she was welcomed by her family, as well as representatives of the Marmara Association for Solidarity with Prisoners’ Families (MATUHAYDER), the Free Women’s Movement (TJA), and the DEM Party (Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party).


Welcomed with chants of “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom), Mengütay said following her release: “As happy as I am, my joy is overshadowed by the fact that I had to leave my friends behind. But we will get them all out soon.”


Referring to the ongoing process for peace and democratic society, Mengütay emphasized her willingness to take part in the new political phase. “As you know, a peace process is underway. We are all part of this process. We are ready to do everything within our power.”


Sentenced by a State Security Court


Mengütay was born in 1974 in a village in the district of Susuz in Kars province and joined the Kurdish freedom movement in 1993. In 1996, she was arrested in Erzurum, charged before a State Security Court (DGM, since abolished) with “destroying the unity of the Turkish state,” and sentenced to life imprisonment.


During her 30 years in prison, she was held in various correctional facilities. Reflecting on her three decades of imprisonment after her release, Mengütay said: “May these 30 years be dedicated to our people.”

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Red-tagging persists even during VP Duterte’s impeachment trial
content:
“It is not terrorism to learn. It is not terrorism to fight for our land.”


CAGAYAN DE ORO — Indigenous rights defenders criticized senator-judge Robinhood Padilla’s remarks during Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial hearing on August 12.


Padilla at the time accused the now-defunct Lumad schools in Davao of being “infiltrated by terrorism.”


Julieta Gomez of the Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas (Katribu) and former ACT Teachers Rep. France Castro debunked his claims. “These [allegations] have been constantly used by Robin Padilla,” Castro said in Filipino during the Bantay Impeachment program of the People’s Alternative Media Network (Altermidya).


In this week’s impeachment trial, Xylene Del Campo, state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU), took the witness stand. She evaluated the responses of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Duterte’s stint as education secretary to the audit observation memorandums and notice of suspension issued in relation to the alleged improper liquidation of confidential funds by both agencies.


State auditor Xylene Del Campo listens to a question of defense lawyer Kristine Ferrer during Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial hearing on August 12, 2026. Photo from the Senate


Read:


State surveillance in schools angers teachers


Padilla asked Del Campo—whose job ensures proper liquidation of public funds—if she was aware of the identification of more than 50 Lumad schools in Davao that were infiltrated by terrorism and the composition of New People’s Army (NPA) members, where there were alleged minors. No questions regarding liquidations were raised by the senator.


Padilla did not mention the name of the Lumad school. However, the number of schools he stated described the number of campuses under the Salugpongan Ta’ Tanu Igkanogon Community Learning Center Incorporated across the Davao region that were forcibly closed during the administration of former President Rodrigo Duterte.


Is the allegation proven?


The then DepEd-recognized Salugpongan learning center was established by the Rural Missionaries of the Philippines (RMP), a church-based organization that served marginalized sectors. It was one of the learning institutions that provided Indigenous education in Mindanao.


Through a resolution, the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) labeled these schools as being established by the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), echoing the report of the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC).


The other schools were the Tribal Filipino Program of Surigao del Sur (Trifps), the Mindanao Interfaith Services Foundation Incorporated (Misfi), the Center for Lumad Advocacy and Services (Clans), and the Alternative Learning Center for Agricultural and Livelihood Development (Alcadev).


In 2015, tribal leaders in Talaingod reportedly requested the stoppage of the Salugpongan operation, citing affidavits of alleged former students who said that they were taught to hate the government and prepared to be part of the NPA.


The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) released its

The Haran Report

 in 2019. It stemmed from two position papers submitted by the Save Our Schools (SOS) Network, an alliance of various organizations advocating for children’s right to education, and the tribal leaders in Talaingod both in 2015. The probe lasted up to the first half of 2018.


Read:

CHR Haran report revisited amid calls to reverse Talaingod 13 conviction


CHR stated in its report that the allegations against the Salugpongan were alarming, saying that DepEd which regulates basic and secondary education has legal grounds to shut down the schools if proven. However, the CHR concluded in its report that DepEd, when it received the letter request from tribal leaders, had not made a “serious investigation.” Citing testimonies from DepEd representatives, the independent commission further stated that the government did not provide an opportunity to Salugpongan officials to contest the intended closure.


“It must be stressed that the IPs (Indigenous peoples), particularly children, including those living outside their communities, have a right to education in their own culture. The temporary closure of the subject facilities, no matter how brief, violated this right,” a part of the CHR report reads.

author: rti_admin
title: We Are Not Your Little Anything: On the Portrayal of Mizoram and the Ethics of Being Seen
content:
You scroll through a reel of Aizawl at dusk. The camera pans across the ridge. Terraced houses cling to the slope, holding on the way our houses do because our land is nearly vertical and there is nowhere else for them to sit. The light is soft. The audio is Japanese, likely a scrap of dialogue pulled from a series or a film and laid over the frame. It is not translating anything; it has no connection to what you are looking at. It is there because it sounds like somewhere else, and that is what aesthetic means now.

I have been thinking about that reel for weeks and about the comments under it. Most of them are from Mizos. Most are proud – feels like Kyoto, little Japan of India, hard to believe this is India. And I have been trying to name precisely what is wrong with the fact that we are the ones cheering.

A recent essay on this platform traced how counterculture and marginalized aesthetics only become palatable once dominant groups appropriate, sanitize or rebrand them. That essay was writing about punk, about Gandhi’s ascetic performance, about the Mary Kom yellowface. I want to extend the argument in a direction the writer only gestures toward – what happens when the aesthetic being consumed is not a jacket or a film but a land, a festival, a woman in puan (traditional Mizo wrap) at Chapchar Kut and the consumers arrive by the trainload.

The friend who stopped being interesting

A friend told me a story recently. She was at her hostel in a mainland university, and a non-Northeast girl came up to her, bright and curious, and asked where she was from. Meghalaya, my friend said. The girl became warm, generous, full of questions. They chatted for a while. Then at dinner, in a group, someone mentioned in passing that Meghalaya is a state in India, the girl went quiet. She stopped speaking to my friend. Over the course of the evening she drifted away, and by the next day she had forgotten my friend existed.

I keep returning to that story because it captures the machinery so cleanly. My friend was interesting when she was foreign. She became invisible the moment she was recategorized as Indian. Nothing about her had changed. What changed was the girl’s calculation of what my friend was worth to her – as an exotic acquaintance, potentially high; as a fellow citizen from a place she considered peripheral, nothing. That transaction is what governs how mainland India encounters the Northeast now and it is what governs the shape of the tourism arriving in Mizoram.

Little Switzerland, Little Japan, Little Anywhere-But-Here

The comparisons come constantly. Little Switzerland. Little Japan. Just like Korea. The whole vocabulary is diminutive. Not Switzerland. Little Switzerland. The mainland viewer is not permitted to see Mizoram as itself. They can only see it as a pocket substitute for somewhere they would rather be, somewhere they cannot afford to fly to. The land is granted value only through comparison and only as a smaller, cheaper, more accessible version of an actual destination.

What this does is protect the viewer from having to revise their mental map. Mizoram is allowed to be beautiful only if that beauty is imported. The moment the beauty is claimed as Indian and Mizo, on its own terms, the frame collapses. That is why you see the second move so often – the pivot to “see, this is India too, not a foreign land.” When someone points out that Aizawl does not honk, that Mizos queue, that the streets are clean, the same voice that a moment ago called it Little Switzerland now insists that this is India, this is us. Both moves are doing the same work. Both are refusing to let Mizoram be Indian and orderly at the same time, because that would force a reckoning with why the places the viewer considers the real India are neither.

The railway reaching Aizawl has been described in the national press as a milestone of connectivity. It is. It is also a distribution system for this gaze at scale. When I first heard the trains were coming, my thought was not about goods or jobs. It was about the tourists. How were we going to handle them, not in the logistical sense. In the sense of what they would do when they arrived believing they had earned access to a curiosity and what we would feel obliged to give them.

At festivals across the Northeast now, videos are circulating of men, tourists from the mainland, grabbing women in traditional attire to pose for photographs. Sometimes the woman is pulled by the arm. Sometimes …

author: Brian Hioe
title: KMT Hits Out At Internet Disruption Drill as “Martial Law”
content:
THE KMT HAS hit out at an Internet slowdown drill, which was conducted during the annual Wan-an drill yesterday. The Wan-an drill is an annual air raid drill in which individuals are called on to shelter in place. This year was the first time that mobile Internet was slowed down, so as to prepare for potential contingencies involving disruptions to Taiwan’s communication networks.

Taiwan is increasingly wary of what might take place if its submarine cables, connecting Taiwan to the rest of the world in terms of Internet, were cut in wartime by Chinese vessels. When this occurred to Taiwan’s outlying island of Matsu in 2023, sending a text message would take 20 minutes. Likewise, China has stepped up grey-zone activity that could potentially allow for the cutting of submarine cables.

Nevertheless, it may not be a surprise that at a time when the KMT has generally taken aim at any defensive measures that would be useful for Taiwan in wartime, whether that be drones or other capabilities, they have also hit out at the Internet slowdown drill. In particular, the KMT sought to tar the Internet drill as some kind of authoritarian measure intended to test capacities to enforce an Internet blackout, claiming that the drill was “False practice, true martial law.”

The DPP framed the slowdown drill as something conducted, too, by other democratic countries in the region such as South Korea and Japan. By contrast, the KMT has pointed to that Internet shutdowns are most commonly carried out by authoritarian countries in order to prevent information from leaking out about atrocities committed during that period.

Indeed, this is not incorrect. The KMT is also not incorrect when it calls on the Lai administration to provide greater clarity about what capacities it specifically hopes to test disruptions to. But it would, of course, be China that would seek to disrupt Taiwan’s Internet in the event of wartime, and such a drill would allow for practicing how to restore capacities–or what needs to be done in order to strengthen resilience. Likewise, the drill would make members of the public more aware of the possibility of disruptions to communication networks in wartime, in that drills are meant to allow the public to imagine what wartime scenarios could look like and to prepare accordingly.

Ironically, the mobile Internet slowdown drill was probably watered down in order to avoid disruption or panicking the public. After all, Wi-Fi Internet was still usable during this time, potentially limiting its ability to test how to restore connectivity in the event of disruptions.

One notes that Taiwan’s civic tech community has long pushed the government on the issue of testing for Internet outages. However, the Taiwanese government was historically reluctant on the matter due to fears that this would ramp up fears about war, affecting Taiwan’s stock market, and potentially leading to electoral blowback against the DPP. In this way, it is surprising that the slowdown drill happened to begin with. But it can be expected that the KMT will attack it nonetheless–further driving home that the party will aim to sabotage any effort by Taiwan to build up capacities that could be useful in wartime.

author: groundxero
title: The Student, The State And The Minority: Historical Continuity In Indian Protest Politics
content:
The en masse participation of Muslims in democratic protests — for justice, equality and well-being for all — will depend on the general public accepting them as fellow citizens.


 


Tashhar Mahmood 


 


Havā mẽ hai jashn, fizā mẽ hai shor


Bhagvē raṅg mẽ liptā huā hai ye daur


Par sōchŏ zarā, dil se pūchhŏ ye bāt


Kyā vāqi’ āzād hai hamārī zāt


 


Kitābõ mẽ likhā hai hamārā deś āzād


Magar har taraf hai vahśat kā ik fasād


 


(

Celebration in the air, clamour in the atmosphere


These times, they are entwined in saffron


But think a bit, ask yourself this question,


Are our people really free?


 


Books tell us our country is free


Yet terrifying chaos engulfs all directions

) 


 


India will celebrate the 80th anniversary of its Independence in a year but people, especially the country’s youth, are still demanding

azadi

 (freedom), freedom from

punjiwad

, freedom from samantwad, freedom from

Manuwad

, freedom from

jatiwad

 … Why? The answer is common knowledge, but very few people dare to spell it out. Education, employment, healthcare, transportation, good governance, justice and all other fields are afflicted with a serious disease, the disease of corruption, binary politics and the “othering” of Muslims. Many, especially those from lower- and middle-class families, are suffering because of rampant corruption, widespread inequality, and the lack of equal and fair opportunities. No wonder students across the country have been demanding that the government fix these problems; they have also been demanding the establishment of a just and accountable system. Their demonstrations reflect the concern of ordinary people, who want positive changes in society and better opportunities for future generations.


 


India won Independence from oppressive British rule in 1947, but many across the social divide have been asking whether we have been able to establish the rule of law even after almost 80 years of Independence. India is a democratic and secular country where the government, since it is elected by the people, is expected to work for the good of the people irrespective of their religion, caste, race and colour. Yet many believe the present government (central and states) has always accorded greater priority to political and religious issues than to everyday problems faced by the people. During elections, some political parties have been using religious and communal issues to influence the electorate while paying little or no attention to education, employment, healthcare, infrastructure development, social welfare and social justice. The growing focus of some political parties on divisive politics has led many, especially students and the youth, to wonder whether public policies are, at all, designed to meet the real needs of society.


 


Protest politics is not a post-Independence phenomenon in India. Its roots can be traced to British colonial rule. During colonial rule, people in India came together to raise their voice against every discriminatory and divisive policy, even though the British administration almost always brutally suppressed such protests. The British rulers arrested and tortured and, in some cases, killed the protesters. Despite this, people across the country continued to demand their rights and freedom. Students have always played a vital role in political movements in India. They have often been among the first to raise social and political issues, and demand justice, because universities and educational institutions, as is their wont, encourage free discussions and debates, and promote critical thinking. In fact, students played a key role in the Independence movement. And after independence, they have stood up for people’s democratic rights, demanded educational reforms and social justice, making significant contributions to political and social change.


 


Ever since the BJP came to power, students of institutions such as the Aligarh Muslim University and Jawaharlal Nehru University have been raising important issues, organizing protests, and demanding that these issues be resolved according to law. In 2019, they faced brutal state action for organizing constitutional protests. One of the major issues seven years ago was the discriminatory Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) and the National Register of Citizens (NRC). These laws and measures triggered extensive protests across the country. Members of the Muslim community felt they were being unfairly targeted …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Prison officials accountable for P7 million missing fund
content:
The Bureau of Corrections should investigate its erring personnel, file the necessary charges and demand that she return what she embezzled instead of squeezing the PDLs dry.

MANILA — Where did the political prisoners’ money go?

Political prisoners and support groups are demanding an investigation into millions of pesos in missing funds belonging to Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) at the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW).

They stressed that prison authorities should hold accountable those responsible instead of passing the burden to inmates.

The controversy emerged after CIW officials disclosed the results of an internal audit that reportedly found a major discrepancy in the institution’s trust fund system where money sent by families to PDLs is deposited and managed by prison authorities.

In a statement released on August 6, political prisoners at CIW said Superintendent Daisy Castillote announced on July 30 that funds entrusted to the institution for PDLs could not be fully accounted for.

According to the prisoners, records showed that the trust fund should contain around P13 million, but an audit found that only about P6 million remained, leaving roughly P7 million unaccounted for.

The political prisoners said the discrepancy did not yet include jewelry and other trust fund accounts not reflected in the system.

For many inmates, the trust fund serves as a lifeline.

CIW limits the amount of cash PDLs may personally hold, prompting families to send money through remittances that prison authorities place in trust accounts from which inmates can withdraw small amounts each week for daily needs.

The prisoners said that they immediately demanded the return of the missing funds. However, they said that prison authorities proposed recovering the lost amount through income generated from inmates’ telephone calls.

Under the proposal, the cost of a five-minute phone call would increase from P3 to P5, while inmates would temporarily lose access to their share of telephone revenues that they previously used for dormitory expenses and other collective needs.

“PDLs were robbed, yet PDLs are being made to pay for it,” CIW political prisoners said in Filipino.

The prisoners also reported problems involving remittances sent through LBC following the announcement, stressing that some inmates did not receive money sent by their families and received no clear explanation from prison personnel.

They called for the immediate return of the funds, the abolition of the trust fund system, and investigations by the Commission on Human Rights, Department of Justice, and Congress.

Former political prisoners and human rights advocates have since joined the calls for accountability.

In a joint statement released on Aug. 12, the Samahan ng mga Ex-Detainee Laban sa Detensyon at Aresto (Selda) and the LAYA Campaign for the Release of All Political Prisoners expressed support for the demands raised by CIW political prisoners.

They criticized proposals to replenish the missing funds through increased telephone charges imposed on inmates.

Selda Vice Chairperson Danilo dela Fuente said that prison authorities should pursue those responsible instead of requiring inmates to shoulder the losses. “The Bureau of Corrections should investigate its erring personnel, file the necessary charges and demand that she return what she embezzled instead of squeezing the PDLs dry.”

LAYA spokesperson Amanda Echanis said that government agencies must conduct an impartial investigation into the missing funds.

“The Commission on Human Rights, the Department of Justice and other pertinent government agencies must get to the bottom of this,” Echanis said. “A thorough and impartial investigation must be done.”

Echanis said that the controversy reflects broader concerns about corruption in government institutions. “While poor Filipino people are easily put in jail, plunderers in government remain in power,” she said. “Accountability must be upheld.”

Beyond recovering the missing money, prisoners and support groups questioned the trust fund system itself.

Political prisoners said that they no longer have confidence in a mechanism that places funds sent by families under the control of prison authorities.

They demanded that inmates regain control over funds intended for their welfare.

Echanis said that money remitted by families should remain under the management of prisoners themselves and should be used solely for their collective needs …

author: Mekong Review 2
title: The cost of visibility Nathalie Chi
content:
Protests against the Chinese mega-embassy in London. Credit: Monkey Butler Images F ace covered, recognisable features hidden. A back-up phone in hand, location services disabled. No recent travel plans. No recent contact with family members in Tibet. Avoid cameras. Avoid interviews. At political protests against the Chinese government, including recent demonstrations against the planned Chinese mega-embassy in London, some Tibetan participants arrive with these calculations already made. Not everyone takes the same precautions, but everyone understands the necessity. Visibility travels, particularly for Tibetans. A single photograph, name, or online post can instantly cross borders, reaching far beyond the crowd standing on a London street. This landscape of fear has recently gained a physical anchor. In January 2026, the UK government approved China’s plan to redevelop the Royal Mint Court in central London into its largest diplomatic mission in Europe. The plan has faced sustained opposition from local residents, campaign groups, and politicians, who have raised concerns over national security, surveillance, protest safety, and the impact on surrounding areas. author: Benjamin Cordero
title: Ang Paglalayag sa Kawalan: Isang Pagsusuri sa The Odyssey (2026)
content:
Isang dambuhalang tagumpay sa sining ng pelikula ang The Odyssey (2026) ni Christopher Nolan. Bagaman napakamahal na ng halaga ng sine sa kasalukuyang panahon, isa itong biswal na hiyas na nararapat panoorin sa pinakamalaking telon hangga’t maaari. Ngunit sa ilalim ng nagngangalit na alon ng Dagat Mediteranyo o sa sindak na dulot ng Cyclops o sa bigat ng modernong pagganap na dala ni Matt Damon, may kuwentong pumipintig sa isang napakapamilyar na paraan.

Ang panonood ng The Odyssey sa pamamagitan ng matang Pilipino ay parang nakararanas ng matinding déjà vu . Para sa isang kulturang hinubog ng pangingibang-bansa, walang-katapusang pagtitiis, at pagkakawatak-watak ng pamilya, ang sampung taong pakikipagsapalaran ni Odysseus para lang makauwi ay hindi lang kuwento ng mitolohiyang Griyego—ito mismo ang buhay at kalagayan ng modernong Pilipino.

Ang pinakamabilis at pinakamatinding koneksyon ng pelikula ni Nolan sa buhay-Pilipino ay ang karakter mismo ni Odysseus. Siya ay isang lalaking nakakulong sa isang walang-awa at nakapapagod na pagpapatapon sa sarili. Sa pelikula, mariing ipinakita ni Nolan ang sikolohikal na epekto ng pagkakahiwalay ni Odysseus sa kanyang bayan; hindi lang siya lumalaban sa mga halimaw, kundi lumalaban din siya sa oras, sa distansya, at sa unti-unting paglaho ng alaala ng tahanang kanyang iniwan.

Ito ang salamin ng totoong buhay ng milyun-milyong Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs), ang ating mga bagong bayani. Katulad ni Odysseus na umalis ng Ithaca para lumaban sa digmaan sa Troy para sa kanyang bayan, ang OFW ay umaalis din sa Pilipinas para lumaban sa isang digmaang pang-ekonomiko sa dayuhang lupain. Pareho silang ginagabayan ng iisang layunin: ang buhayin, protektahan, at sa huli ay balikan ang pamilyang kanilang minamahal.

Kapag nakatulala si Odysseus (Matt Damon) sa karagatan habang nakakulong sa isla ng Ogygia, sinumang Pilipinong nanonood ay makikita ang mukha ng ating mga tita, tito, ina, at ama na nagpupuyat habang nakatingin sa bintana ng mga matataas na gusali sa Hong Kong, Dubai, o Singapore. Ang mga halimaw na hinarap ni Odysseus—ang mapanlinlang na akit ni Circe o ang nakaparalisang pagkalimot na dala ng mga Lotus-Eater—ay madaling maitumbas sa mga panganib ng pangingibang-bansa ngayon: (1) Ang tuksong makiangkop nang tuluyan sa dayuhang kultura at limutin ang sariling pinagmulan. (2) Ang mabigat at mapag-isang depresyon ng pagiging dayuhan sa ibang bansa at; (3) Ang mga burukrasya, kahirapan sa bayang babalikan at pisikal na hadlang na nagpapatagal sa pag-uwi nang maraming taon, o dekada.

Habang nakikipaglaban si Odysseus sa malalaking alon, ang bigat ng emosyon ng pelikula ay pasan naman nina Penelope (Anne Hathaway) at Telemachus (Tom Holland) sa Ithaca. Mahusay na ipinakita ni Nolan na ang Ithaca ay hindi isang marangyang kaharian na naghihintay sa kanilang hari, kundi isang gumuguhong bahay na kinatatawanan ng mga mapagsamantalang manliligaw/dayuhan na unti-unting nagpapasasa sa kanilang yaman.

Ang bahaging ito ng kuwento ay napakasakit tanggapin para sa mga pamilyang Pilipino. Kapag ang isang magulang ay umalis ng Pilipinas para magtrabaho sa abroad, ang pamilyang naiwan ay parang nakabinbin sa hangin. Si Penelope ang sumasalamin sa nakatutunaw at mapag-isang dusa ng asawang naiwan—na kadalasan ay ang ina na mag-isang nagtataguyod sa bahay, nagpoprotekta sa mga anak laban sa mga mapagsamantalang tao sa lipunan, at nagkukunwaring matatag kahit na nadudurog ang puso sa tindi ng pangungulila.

Si Telemachus naman ang kumakatawan sa “anak ng OFW.” Ipinakita ni Tom Holland ang isang binatang puno ng kumplikadong emosyon—may galit, may pangungulila, at may matinding pressure. Lumaki siya sa ilalim ng anino ng isang tanyag na ama na halos hindi niya matandaan, at napilitang ipagtanggol ang kanilang tahanan bago pa siya maging handa. Sa pang-araw-araw na buhay ng Pilipino, ito ang realidad ng milyun-milyong bata na lumalaki sa pamamagitan lamang ng video calls at remittance slips. Lumalaki silang walang ama o ina sa tabi, napipilitang magmatured nang maaga, nakalantad sa nauusong karahasan (maging sa sariling paaralan) at pasan ang bigat ng sakripisyo ng magulang habang nahihirapan ding kilalanin ang sarili.

Sa kaibuturan nito, ang The Odyssey ay isang paggalugad sa konsepto ng nostos—ang sinaunang salitang Griyego para sa pagbabalik-bayan. Sa kulturang Pilipino, ito ang ating pinakamalalim na mithiin: ang konsepto ng pagbabalik o pag-uwi.

author: Kevin Lin
title: The Seven Deadly Sins of Conferencing
content:
Many of us know from experience that the most memorable and enjoyable parts of participating in a conference are the tea and coffee breaks, the conversations lunches and dinners, the informal chats outside of the conference room while the meeting is still happening, and the late-night hangouts with other participants. Genuinely good conversations take place and relationships are formed or renewed in those moments. So why don’t we recognise what is obvious, and create structures that bring out these experiences?


Social movements rely on purposeful gatherings to connect, share experiences, and strategise. We do this so often we should be really good at it. But more often than not, things do not seem to quite work. This has prompted me to reflect, and then test my impressions with other conference-goers who turn out to be feeling much the same ways. I need to first acknowledge how much unseen labour goes into any event planning; the event organisers are the most invisible if everything goes well. But it is necessary to recognise and name things that do not seem to work.


Here are the seven deadly sins of conference organising. I want to speak to my fellow conference organisers: of course, not all of us committed all of the sins, and some of you have done much better. But many of the sins would sound familiar to us, and we often let our guards down. By naming them, we may do a better job at avoiding them, and get to organise and experience more effective, creative and joyful gatherings.


 


Greed


 


The first sin is greed. We are often greedy about what can be accomplished with a gathering, especially with sizable conferences. We want to invite many people to be there to meet and connect, while also want them to have substantial discussions.


A medium to large conference of dozens to a few hundred people is amazing. But it is not primarily a place for deep learning or for substantial conversations despite our best efforts and most sincere wishes. There are simply too many sessions, too many speakers and too many people to learn and engage deeply. We listen to one panel after another and hardly remember anything from each speaker, while facilitators apologise for running out of time and no more time for questions. We then try to have conversations during breaks that on average last for 5 to 10 minutes before rushing back to the next session or talking or introducing ourselves to someone else. You should not feel alone in experiencing this.


We know deep learning and substantial conversation are most likely to take place in much smaller meetings. You may really have to keep it to a very small number of participants, arguably no more than 10 or 15 but maybe even fewer, to have sustained conversations that give everyone time to think, allow ideas to develop, and for them to build on each other’s ideas.


The medium and large conferences serve other important goals: it is good for building new relationships or renewing old ones, for feeling part of a larger movement with many others with shared values and goals, and for experiencing the optimism and joy of movement-building. It is good enough to take away with you the connections you have made, a sense of the movement’s diversity and creativity, and the fact that people are doing the best they can under enormous pressure and risk.


If these are the realistic goals, then our task is to structure the events in ways that let people and ideas to breath, to have both structured discussions and unstructured time for spontaneous conversations, and to make these events into festivals.


 


Busyness


 


The second sin is busyness. Far too often, I have been in conference planning where the logistics – the venue search and booking, the travel arrangement, the drinks, snacks and meals, and the interpretation – take up most of the planning time. We end up spending very little time discussing and experimenting with the actual program. In fact, the program design at times feels like an afterthought.


The logistics discussions and preparations are often not completely done until the very last minute. Time for a program discussion tends to be squeezed in between logistics discussions. When we are tight on time, we tend to revert to the familiar and the safest: let us get these speakers speakers for these panels, and each speaks for 15 minutes. It is the least that can go wrong. No one can claim they love this, but we keep doing it anyway.


It may be worth aiming to reserve a …

author: Rojava IC
title: Sleeper-Cell Report June 2026 – Justice Palace Department’s Head Killed
content:
The head of the Palace of Justice was seriously injured after being targeted in an attack on June 16. 


 


Key Points 


Five sleeper cell attacks were recorded in June; a slight increase from only three in May


A total of four military personnel were killed, and at least two injured 


Fatalities of two suspected ISIS affiliates were also recorded


Paper leaflets containing Pro-ISIS propaganda were distributed in several provinces throughout Syria


 


In Depth


This month, RIC recorded a total five attacks, two of which have been directly claimed by ISIS at the time of writing, the remaining three are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.


On June 15, unidentified gunmen believed to be of an ISIS cell attacked the headquarters of general security forces, two of its members were killed and several others injured, west of Raqqa city, before one of the attackers self-detonated.  


On June 16, Salah Ahmad al-Saleh, head of the Palace of Justice in the town of Babila in rural Damascus was seriously injured by an explosive device attached to his vehicle. And on the same day, ISIS members targeted an oil tanker with machine-gun fire near the northern city of Manbij. Material damage to the tanker was reported.


On June 20, unidentified gunmen believed to be part of an ISIS cell, attacked members of the 76th Armored Division, causing the death of two Division’s members. The attack occurred near Tahnah junction in the western countryside of Manbij.


On June 24, two gunmen believed to be ISIS members, on a motorcycle opened fire on two members of the Engineering Regiment of the 72nd Division, on Ain Issa Road in Raqqa countryside, injuring both of them. 


On June 19, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) forces conducted an airstrike in northwest Syria. CENTCOM confirmed the killing of Ali Husayn al-‘Ulaywi, a senior ISIS leader. 


Paper leaflets were distributed in several mosques across different areas in Daraa, Idlib and Aleppo provinces. The leaflets contain extremist content and rhetoric linked to ISIS.


Save the Children, an Australian children’s advocacy organization, called for the return of an ISIS-linked Australian woman and her disabled child from Syria after a failed repatriation attempt. Following the failed departure, Syrian authorities reportedly transferred them to a detention facility in northwestern Syria’s Idlib Governorate, since then, her family lost contact with her.


Another Australian woman was accused of supporting ISIS and appeared before a court in Melbourne, where prosecutors alleged she lived in a household that held a teenage girl in slavery while the victim was subjected to repeated abuse.  Her request for bail was rejected, as prosecutors argued she poses a risk to public safety. 


Tammy Bruce, U.S. Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations Ambassador said that it would continue working with Syria to combat ISIS, and support efforts to preserve stability and safety in the country.

title: TJK-E condemns sexual assault against German activist in custody in Istanbul, calls for legal action
content:
In January 2026, a delegation of several youth organisations – including journalists – as well as other human rights/peace activists travelled to the Kurdish areas in Turkey. Their goal was to observe the protests against the military escalation in Syria and bring them into the public eye. The delegation was on its way to the Turkish-Syrian border as part of the ‘Peoples’ Caravan – Caravan for the Defense of Humanity’. There they wanted to express their solidarity with the people in the city of Kobane. The group, however, was arrested by the police and the participants of the delegation exposed serious violations by Turkish officials. According to statements, there was massive violence during the deportation process. Members of the delegation also reported being subjected to physical and psychological violence, sleep deprivation, insults, and threats.


German activist Paula Maier, one of the internationalists taking part in the campaign, announced that she was raped by a Turkish official while being held at a detention center in Istanbul in January.

Enternasyonalist dayanışmayı hedef alan gözaltı şiddetini, tecavüzü ve baskıları teşhir ediyoruz.

pic.twitter.com/Q3uV1p1rp9


— Tevgera Jinên Azad (@NavendTJA)

August 14, 2026


In a written statement denouncing the violence against internationalist activists, the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E) said the following:


“The male mentality that wages war against women has, throughout history, manifested itself most starkly through attacks on women’s dignity and bodies. Through violence, femicide, rape, and psychological attacks, domination is imposed on women, while attempts are made to control their lives, their will, and their bodies.


The arrest of activist Paula Maier, who was part of an international delegation opposing the attacks on Rojava, and the sexual assault she was subjected to at a deportation center in Istanbul demonstrate how this patriarchal mentality is reflected through the mechanisms of the state. This should not be treated merely as an isolated incident, but must be assessed within the broader context of the systematic dimensions of violence and repression against women.


As TJK-E, we have been fighting against this mentality for years and have made our position against the male-dominated state mentality of power and domination unequivocally clear. We stress that what happened must be fully investigated through legal channels, those responsible must be identified, and the necessary legal action must be taken.


A mentality that seeks to evade responsibility for violence against women by hiding behind state mechanisms is unacceptable. The use of state mechanisms must not mean covering up what happened or protecting the perpetrators. On the contrary, it is the state’s responsibility to ensure that such incidents are fully investigated and that those responsible are held accountable before the law.


The massacres and policies of violence directed against women in the 21st century are a manifestation of the patriarchal system’s efforts to preserve its own existence. We must intensify our struggle to bring an end to this war against women’s rights, freedom, and will. Holding the perpetrators and those responsible legally accountable will be one of the fundamental measures of ensuring justice and bringing the truth to light.


This system, which targets the lives, freedom, and dignity of thousands of women and seeks to establish control over women’s bodies and will, will undoubtedly one day be dismantled.


In the 21st century, the women’s struggle advancing on the basis of women’s freedom will continue to grow stronger in its resistance to the patriarchal and dominant system. Through the struggle of organized women, the voices of women who have been taken from us and whose voices have been silenced will be heard once again, and justice and truth will be brought to light.


As TJK-E, we once again affirm that we will resolutely continue our struggle against all forms of violence against women, femicide, and the male-dominated state mentality.”

author: James McVicar
title: Students teach Hanson a lesson
content:
Across the country yesterday, students walked out of their schoolrooms and lecture halls and flooded into the streets to protest against Pauline Hanson and her far-right political project.

As many as 4,000 marched in Sydney. Two thousand in Perth and Adelaide and 1,000 in Brisbane. In Canberra, 500 students protested at the Australian National University campus and 200 turned out in Wollongong. High schoolers spontaneously organised protests in Shoalhaven, Lismore, and Albury. In Melbourne, where I was, the march was colossal—about 5,000 people—and the mood was absolutely electric.

The chants rang out with righteous rage: “Too young to protest? We call bullshit!” and “High school, uni, teachers too; Pauline Hanson, we’re coming for you!” Undoubtedly the most popular was a two-word refrain: “Fuck Pauline!” Sometimes less is more.

The homemade placards were funny and indignant and withering. “I love naps but I stay woke”. “Still got a better attendance rate than Hanson”. “Orange is the new evil”. On the ground I spotted a papier-mache Hanson head that, from the looks of it, had had a run-in with a few too many shiny black shoes.

Anyone over the age of 25 knows what it’s like to be roasted by teenagers. Gen Z sarcasm is one of the most devastating weapons humankind has ever known. So just try to imagine how Hanson must be feeling right now.

All she could muster as a response was a post on X: “If you want to protest something, protest why your parents’ wages are going backwards and the cost of everything is going up ... Whether you know it or not, One Nation and I are fighting for you”. Please don’t hurt me, kids, I’m actually on your side! Pathetic.

The students were protesting against the increasing entrenchment of far-right politics in Australia being spearheaded by Hanson and One Nation. It’s clear to them that Hanson’s reactionary agenda only serves the big end of town. It’s not just Gina Rinehart: more and more wealthy backers are swinging in behind One Nation.

Hanson’s project to demonise migrants and attack the rights of women and workers helps to prop up a society where the few rule over the many. Odessa, a High School Anti-Capitalists member from Huntingtower, hit the nail on the head in her speech: “We know she’s a servant for the wealthy”.

At the same time, the mainstream parties have ceded more and more ground to One Nation. The Liberals are doing their level best to rebrand as One Nation in neckties. Labor politicians are planning to announce substantial cuts to migration. They too want to run a system based on extreme wealth inequality, hard borders and minority rule, so we cannot count on them to stand up to the far right.

One Nation’s rise is part of a broader global shift in politics. Aero, an international student at RMIT and member of Socialist Alternative, spoke about President Javier Milei in Argentina, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in Italy, Nigel Farage in the UK and Donald Trump in America. Students know what’s going on abroad and know it needs to be fought. “Australia does not need our own orange clown”, read one placard.

Around the world, capitalism has less and less to offer people but wage cuts and declining living standards. As governments pour more and more money into war preparations, welfare and social spending are being slashed. The far-right’s authoritarian politics, their championing of social hierarchy and oppression—it all fits the bill for our rulers.

In the middle of the State Library forecourt, the haughty statue of Supreme Court judge and first chancellor of Melbourne University Redmond Barry became a rostrum for unruly teens calling out “Pauline Hanson is a fascist!” Old Redmond would have had a fit. The other two statues outside the State Library—St George slaying a dragon on one side and a triumphant Joan of Arc on the other—seemed a little more the vibe of the day.

This was a protest of students from schools and universities across the country, but the high schoolers were the heroes of the day. I spoke to students from Melbourne High who reckoned there were 40 of them marching. Another 50 from both Northcote High and Coburg High. There were thousands more, including students from as far away as Geelong, Ballarat and Bendigo. Sixty schools were represented at the Sydney rally. In Perth, rally organisers say students from 120 different schools contacted them about joining the strike.

Plenty of high schoolers had to fight for their right to even be there in the …
