title: Four Months of Incarceration Without Trial: Workers and Activists Arrested During Noida Protests Make Glacial Progress Towards Bail
content:
While most of the over 170 people named in the at least 14 FIRs filed in relation to the matter—one of the more controversial aspects of the police action, as filing multiple FIRs in the same criminal action is illegal as per Indian law—are out on bail, the eight prominent activists charged with ‘criminal conspiracy’ continue to remain imprisoned as the judicial process for their release moves along at a snail’s pace.


 


New Delhi, 11 August 2026


 


Mouli Sharma


 


A third of a year has passed since the UP police began a wave of mass arrests to quickly clamp down on a growing worker’s agitation in the state’s industrial hub, Noida. Over 170 people were named in nearly 400 incidents across at least 14 FIRs in the matter, with allegations ranging from destruction of property, criminal conspiracy to outright attempt to murder. 


 


Meanwhile, despite widespread allegations of police brutality, excess, sexual assault, and procedural violations by the UP police, no FIRs till date have been registered against the officers of the UP police, CRPF and SWAT teams involved, nor against the hundreds of industrial giants operating in the region that were evidently in violation of minimum wage and other labour laws for over a decade. 


 


Every month since the first recorded arrests took place on 11 April 2026, when four activists, including three women, were abducted (there was no warrant or cognisable offence involved, and even if there was, male officers aren’t allowed to arrest women in India, and their detention, even by female officers after sundown is outlawed per the Supreme Court’s landmark sundown judgment) by uniformed and ununiformed male police officers from within the Botanical Garden Metro Station, a coalition of the friends, family, and civilians in solidarity with those allegedly being targeted by the state has organised protests and public meetings to ensure the visibility of the continued incarcerations. In August, as in the months before, this coalition, called the Campaign for the Release of Workers and Activists of Noida (CaRWAN) organised a protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar demanding the release of all political prisoners, workers, and activists illegally arrested in Noida workers protest. 


 


“Following their usual script given to them by their masters, the Delhi Police did not allowed peaceful protesters to enter Jantar Mantar citing “threat to law and order” as an excuse, and imposed BNSS 163,” CaRWAN said, referring to a pattern of preventive police action that has followed their solidarity demonstrations since April. The use, or abuse, of section 163 of the BNSS (or section 144 of the erstwhile CrPC), which empowers District Magistrates to impose temporary or special restrictions on public gatherings, meetings and processions has been the subject of controversy for quite some time in the country. The Indian Supreme Court has warned against its casual, excessive, or extra-procedural use, but time and again, the provision has been employed without due process (which requires lengthy bureaucratic formalities, the issuances of public notices, and most crucially, gazetted evidence of its necessity) by successive governments to obstruct protests and civil agitation, and the BJP administration is no different. 


 


In June, too, as this reporter witnessed, security forces deployed at the Jantar Mantar protest site were recalcitrant to permit the monthly demonstration, and forced the gathering of fewer than thirty people to disperse within an hour after having it postponed from 11 in the morning to near 2 in the afternoon. Come August, this hostility seems to have escalated, and the protest on Tuesday was allegedly outright ‘disallowed’ by the police through the use of section 163, citing proximity to 15

th

 August.


 


“Delhi Police tried to stop the protest by threatening the protestors with FIRs and detentions. They called the assembly ‘unlawful’ and tried to hassle the protestors. However, the protestors were undeterred and said that the Delhi Police did not care about the law when the goons of UP police in civil clothes abducted students from Delhi violating all laws regarding inter state arrests without any warrants or notice,” CaRWAN said, referring again to the allegations of procedural violation against the UP police, which gained traction through the social media and viral footage of policemen threatening and even beating unarmed civilians during their so-called security …

author: Mag
title: Tarifrunde im Handel 2026: Zusammen handeln. Für bessere Tarife!
content:
Dossier


„

Tarifrunde im Handel gestartet: ver.di fordert spürbare Lohnerhöhungen über der Inflation, mehr Vollzeitstellen und eine stärkere Tarifbindung. Für rund 5,2 Millionen Beschäftigte im Einzel-, Versand-, Groß- und Außenhandel beginnt ab April 2026 eine entscheidende Entgeltrunde

…“

ver.di-Sonderseite


 mit Nachrichten zur Tarifrunde im Handel 2026 auch aus den Ländern mit unterschiedlichen Forderumngen i.d.R.um 7 Prozent mehr Lohn, mindestens 225 Euro… Siehe hier nur die bundesweiten Aktivitäten:


Mit Hamburg hat der 5. verdi-Tarifbezirk den Pilotabschluss im bayerischen Groß- und Außenhandel übernommen, also weit weg von „mindestens 250 Euro im Monat“


Tarifrunde Groß- und Außenhandel Hamburg: Tarifeinigung für 60.000 Beschäftigte erzielt


„

Das Verhandlungsergebnis orientiert sich am zuvor bundesweit ersten Abschluss im bayerischen Groß- und Außenhandel und sieht eine Entgeltsteigerung von 2,9 Prozent ab 1. August 2026 sowie eine weitere Erhöhung um 2,1 Prozent ab 1. Mai 2027 vor. Die Ausbildungsvergütungen steigen um 40 Euro ab 1. August 2026 und um weitere 30 Euro ab 1. August 2027. Die Laufzeit des Tarifvertrags beträgt 24 Monate

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 11.08.2026 bei ver.di Hamburg

 


Tarifabschluss reißt Lohnuntergrenze


„

In Hamburg hat der fünfte Verdi-Tarifbezirk den Pilotabschluss für den Groß- und Außenhandel übernommen. Das Ergebnis birgt einige Probleme für die Gewerkschaft


Klappe, die fünfte. Nach Bayern, Baden-Württemberg, Rheinland-Pfalz und NRW hat mit Hamburg nun der nächste Verdi-Bezirk im Fachbereich Handel einen Tarifabschluss im Groß- und Außenhandel erzielt. Vorlage der am Dienstag in der Hansestadt getroffenen Einigung ist wie schon in den Bezirken zuvor der Pilotabschluss in Bayern. »Die Verhandlungen waren schwierig«, erklärte Heike Lattekamp, die örtliche Verdi-Verhandlungsführerin für den Groß- und Außenhandel. Am Ende sei es doch »gelungen, eine Einigung zu erzielen«. Entscheidend dafür sei die Bereitschaft der Beschäftigten gewesen, »gemeinsam für ihre Forderungen einzustehen«, zitierte eine Mitteilung der Gewerkschaft. »Ohne den Druck aus den Betrieben wäre dieses Ergebnis nicht möglich gewesen«, pflichtete ihr demnach auch Jan Görbitz aus der Tarifkommission bei. »Wir haben gemeinsam eine spürbare Verbesserung erreicht.«


Ob diese allerdings bei allen Kolleginnen und Kollegen wirklich spürbar wird, ist fraglich. Von den ursprünglich von Verdi geforderten sieben Prozent mehr Entgelt, mindestens aber 250 Euro im Monat, bleibt nicht mehr viel übrig. Die Laufzeit des Tarifvertrags wird doppelt so lang ausfallen wie ursprünglich gefordert und entspricht mit 24 Monaten jener aus dem Pilotabschluss in Bayern. Ebenfalls dementsprechend sollen die Löhne und Gehälter der rund 60.000 Beschäftigten im hamburgischen Großhandel ab August um 2,9 Prozent angehoben werden. Eine weitere Erhöhung der Löhne und Gehälter um 2,1 Prozent soll ab dem 1. Mai 2027 erfolgen. Azubis sollen der Regelung zufolge ab August 40 Euro mehr erhalten, weitere 30 Euro gibt es dann ab August 2027 monatlich obendrauf, teilte Verdi am Dienstag mit.


Die erzielte Erhöhung für die in Lehre befindlichen Kolleginnen und Kollegen entspricht ebenfalls knapp der Hälfte der von Verdi geforderten 150 Euro. Zudem liegt die Erhöhung nur knapp über der Ende Juli vom Statistischen Bundesamt ausgegebenen Schätzung von 2,8 Prozent Inflation. Angesichts zu erwartender Spätfolgen des Iran-Kriegs und der Blockade der Straße von Hormus ist aktuell nicht absehbar, ob eine gut zweiprozentige Erhöhung die Verbraucherpreisentwicklung im kommenden Jahr auffangen kann. Auch stehen für die Beschäftigten Nullmonate im Ergebnis – Mai, Juni und Juli. Für die Zeit der laufenden Tarifverhandlungen seit Ende April gehen die Beschäftigten leer aus – ein Umstand, den Verdi während der Gesprächsrunden als inakzeptabel zurückgewiesen hatte.


Und es gibt noch ein Problem in dem bayerischen Pilotabschluss. Denn sollte dieser in einigen Tarifgebieten übernommen werden, würden Lohngruppen ab Januar 2027 unterhalb des gesetzlichen Mindestlohns von 14,90 Euro fallen. Im Tarifgebiet Berlin-Brandenburg gibt es Beschäftigte mit Berufsausbildung in mehreren Entgeltgruppen, die mit dem Abschluss nicht auf das stündliche Mindestsalär kommen. »Um Unternehmen und Mitarbeitenden dennoch so schnell wie möglich Rechtssicherheit durch einen gültigen Tarifabschluss bieten zu können, wurde im vorliegenden Abschluss die Lohngruppe L1 unter 18 Jahren …

title: Vigil against the geothermal power plant in Varto enters its 102nd day
content:
The vigil launched against the Geothermal Energy Power Plant (JES) project planned by US-based IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim A.Ş. in the village of Xwarik, in Varto (Gimgim), in the province of Muş, entered its 102nd day.


On the 101st day of the vigil, banners reading “We are defending our nature, our beliefs and our future” and “We do not want a geothermal power plant in Varto. Keep your hands off our land, our soil” were hung at the vigil site by the Gimgim Ecology Platform Youth Assembly.


Members of the Ecology Platform are continuing the vigil, drawing attention to the threat posed by the geothermal power plant project to the region’s nature, living spaces and future.


Support for the Licik resistance


As the vigil continued, members of the Gimgim Ecology Platform Youth Assembly expressed their support for the resistance in the village of Licik, in the Karlıova (Kanîreş) district of Bingöl (Çewlig), against an attempt by the company carrying out the geothermal power plant project to begin work there.


The ecology activists travelled to the village of Licik, where they met with local residents resisting the project.

author: Unknown
title: Licik resistance against JES: Words are over, the struggle begins
content:
Resistance continues in the village of Licik, located on the border between the Gimgim (Varto) district of Mûş and the Kanîreş (Karlıova) district of Çewlîg (Bingöl), against the Geothermal Energy Power Plant (JES) planned by Germany-based IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim A.Ş.


Despite the ongoing legal proceedings and the court ruling that is expected, company officials attempted to enter the village with construction machinery accompanied by gendarmes and begin work. However, following the determined resistance of villagers and environmentalists and intensive negotiations, the company officials were forced to back down. The construction machinery was removed from the site.


Following the company’s retreat, a mass protest was held today in Licik village. The protest was attended by the Gimgim, Çêrme and Kanîreş ecology platforms, provincial and district representatives of the DEM Party and DBP, DEM Party Ecology and Agriculture Commission Co-Spokesperson Melis Tartar, and numerous people from surrounding villages.


Despite heavy rain, the crowd gathered in the village centre and marched toward the site of the geothermal power plant project chanting slogans. Following the march, representatives of organizations and villagers held a press statement at the company’s site.


The security forces should defend the people, not the company


Canfidal Boldaş, secretary of the Bingöl branch of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) Coordination Board, said it was unacceptable for the security forces to clear the way for the company before the legal proceedings had been completed.


Pointing out that the project is located at the centre of the living areas, Boldaş said: “What the public authorities should be doing is not surrounding the village and defending the company, but removing the construction machinery from the village until a court ruling is issued. This is a living area very close to agricultural land and barns; it poses a major risk in terms of air, water and soil pollution. This company will leave, but we, the people of Licik, will remain here. We will continue to defend our living spaces.”


The first step on the path to peace is to stop the destruction of nature


DEM Party Ecology Assembly Co-Spokesperson Melis Tartar said companies could not sacrifice villagers’ land for long-term investments. Describing what was happening as a “chain of crimes,” Melis Tartar said: “First they extract and pollute the water through drilling, poison the air and nature, and then they force people into exile. At a time when the peace process is being discussed, are you going to leave people with villages that no longer exist or poisoned air? The first step of this peace process must be precisely to stop the economic and ecological destruction projects here.”


The company is putting on a show of force


Lawyer Kübra Sudan said the case, which has been ongoing for approximately a year, had reached a critical stage and that a decision had recently been made to conduct an on-site inspection. Saying that they expected a decision to suspend the execution of the project following the inspection, Sudan stated that the company’s entry onto the site without waiting for the court’s decision amounted to creating an unlawful fait accompli.


Sudan said: “The company has tried to enter by using the power of the security forces to threaten and intimidate local residents. This intervention while the trial is ongoing is a show of force and is unlawful. On the day of the inspection that will take place in the coming months, we will once again defend our land here. We are the ones who are right, and in the end, we will definitely win.”


Words are over, the struggle begins


Çayan Dursun, a member of the Varto Ecology Platform, drew attention to the importance of resistance on the ground alongside the legal struggle. “We are at a point where international companies do not recognize the law. We are at the point where words end and the struggle begins,” Dursun said, noting that the geothermal power plant project was intended to be built immediately next to residential areas.


Dursun said: “When our air and water are poisoned tomorrow, we will have nowhere left to live. We will once again be forced onto the roads of migration, as we were in the 1990s. We now have to stop merely talking and physically stand in front of the construction machinery.”

title: Karasu: Failure to mention Abdullah Öcalan’s position in 'Framework Law' is a shortcoming
content:
KCK Executive Council Member Mustafa Karasu took part in a special programme broadcast on Medya Haber TV, where he offered important assessments of the “Framework Law” prepared as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process and how the process should move forward.


We publish the first part of this in-depth interview. 


After quite a long time, the ‘Framework Law’ drafted by the government has been submitted to Parliament. How do you assess this ‘Framework Law’ that pertains to Parliament?


It has been awaited for months, as it has truly been the subject of much debate. There were also lengthy discussions on this matter with Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan]. Our people, the democratic forces, the DEM Party, and we have all expressed our views on this law. In fact, it is a long-overdue law. Even if we were to start the process on February 27, 2025 – since Rêber Apo issued his call for Peace and Democratic Society – a year and a half has passed since that day. Such a law could easily have been enacted. This reflects the fact that the AKP government and the state are not sufficiently prepared – or have failed to demonstrate a resolute will – regarding democratization and the resolution of the Kurdish issue on a non-conflictual basis, in line with a legal and political solution. This must be stated clearly. Otherwise, why wouldn’t such a law have been passed within one and a half years? While this law has many aspects that need to be criticized, it marks the beginning of a new path. That marks its significance.


After all, there were discussions about resolving the Kurdish question through democratic and political means without conflict. That is essentially how we viewed this process. The call for Peace and Democratic Society put forward by Rêber Apo was also along these lines. It was a call made public with the knowledge of state officials. That call is clear: the issue is the Kurdish issue. Whatever label is to be used, for us the protection of the unity of society is paramount. There has been a century-long rift between the Turkish state and the Kurds. The purpose of a democratic-political solution is to bridge this rift. This is our approach. We have stated that we have ended the armed struggle. We have stated that we will engage in democratic-political struggle – and not on an individual level, but in a collectively organized form. We have also stated that we will carry out a democratic-political struggle as part of our new strategy. Rêber Apo has already responded by shifting the focus to a legal and political framework. This law must be viewed as a step towards a legal and political solution and as the beginning of entering a political process. A step has been taken at this point.


As Rêber Apo said, even a thousand-kilometer-long journey begins with a single step. That is how we assess it. Otherwise, this law is not one that solves the Kurdish issue or brings a solution. But it must be viewed as the first step of an approach whose goal and purpose is precisely that. The fact that it does not mention the Kurdish issue – and that it is not a law that sets forth a solution to the Kurdish issue or reveals the Kurdish reality – is, of course, a significant shortcoming. We have already addressed this in our statement. But it is a start now. How will we move this start forward? The process from here on out is important. The approaches taken from here on out are important. Will we truly move this forward? Will this help begin progress? Or will this begin a slow down, as it has over the past year and a half or two years, failing to proceed with the necessary speed and determination? Time will tell, of course. From our perspective, we definitely want to bring this process to a successful conclusion. Our resolve is in this direction. The state’s approach can be evaluated as such or such. We are already evaluating it. But from our perspective, the law has been enacted. From now on, we will look ahead. We will do our part to ensure that this initial step leads to a resolution based on democratization and the resolution of the Kurdish issue.


As you mentioned, there has already been a statement by the leadership of your movement. While highlighting the importance of the law, there had also been criticisms in that statement. Can you more precisely formulate what you criticize about the presented laws?


Let’s emphasize this once again. Peace begins first and foremost with according rhetoric. This is decisive. What we are …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Uber Eats Pay Calculation Dispute Reflects Familiar Issues
content:
THE NATIONAL DELIVERY INDUSTRY UNION has filed a lawsuit against Uber Eats for underpaying workers delivering multiple orders at once, a practice referred to as “stacked orders”.

In particular, delivery workers have accused Uber Eats of using unlawful payment calculation formulas, citing cases in which workers were only paid for the delivery time of one order, rather than both orders that they were handling at the time. This would violate new regulations that took effect on July 21st, which require not only hourly compensation at a rate of 245 NT per hour, a wage 1.25 times the minimum wage, as well as at least a minimum payment of 45 NT per order. The new laws were hailed by the Taiwan Delivery Industry Union Alliance and the National Delivery Industrial Union as a victory after six-and-a-half years of campaigning when they were passed earlier this year.

Specifically, food delivery workers began to organize in 2021 and called for the formation of a nationwide delivery workers union. This was in reaction to new salary calculation formulas announced by both Uber Eats and Foodpanda that would have cut their salaries by 10% to 30%. While workers could have made between 65 NT and 75 NT on a delivery last year, now workers will make between 43 NT and 50 NT on the same delivery. As such, workers will need to work more hours while making less pay. According to Chen Yu-an, one of the union conveners, while he previously made 9,600 NT by delivering 110 orders in a week, after the changes, he made 9,000 NT by delivering 164 orders.

Workers were critical of the fact that these changes, which severely affect their livelihood, were announced without consultation with workers by Uber Eats or Foodpanda. As such, they criticized the new salary calculation formulas as decided through a “black box.”

Likewise, the changes were criticized as increasing the odds of accidents for delivery workers. The average rate of accidents in central Taiwan for delivery workers increased from 1.4 times per month to 4 times a month after the new changes in salary calculation were implemented in 2021. Workers then called for accident compensation to be raised to at least 100,000 NT.

It appears that industry union groups have been attentive to the possibility that Uber Eats would try to circumvent the new laws. One notes that Uber’s entrance into the Taiwanese market as a ride-sharing service was a contested one to begin with, with Uber registering as a software company and not a taxi company to try and evade regulation as a taxi company, and racking up continual fines because of its refusal to stop operating in Taiwan. This is part of what originally led to the shift toward Uber providing food delivery services in Taiwan, seeing as legal challenges prevented Uber drivers from directly operating as a ride-sharing service. Eventually, a compromise was found with Uber registering as a taxi company.

Yet with Uber facing resistance from local taxi unions at that point in time, Uber sought to frame the issue as one in which the Taiwanese government was failing to adapt to trends in global innovation, through its failure to make way for Uber. Consequently, Uber sought to depict taxi unions as conservative forces bent on preventing innovation, thereby miring Uber in old frameworks of employment. Indeed, the rise of the “gig economy” has allowed companies such as Uber, Foodpanda, and others to skirt regulations by framing worker exploitation as technological innovation. It can be expected that union groups will continue to act to provide oversight over the company, then.

title: Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nde Ebola salgını: Can kaybı 2 bini aştı
content:
Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti’nde (KDC) Ebola salgını ağırlaşarak devam ediyor. Sağlık Bakanlığının açıkladığı son verilere göre, salgının başlangıcından bu yana 4 bin 449 doğrulanmış vaka tespit edilirken, 2 bin 61 kişi hayatını kaybetti.

Salgında 886 kişinin ise iyileştiği bildirildi. Böylece Ebola nedeniyle ölüm oranı yüzde 46,3 olarak güncellendi.

KDC Sağlık Bakanlığı, salgının Haut-Uele, Ituri, Kuzey Kivu, Güney Kivu ve Tshopo olmak üzere beş eyalette etkisini sürdürdüğünü açıkladı.

Toplam 53 bölgeye yayılan salgının merkez üssü Ituri eyaleti olmaya devam ediyor. Güney Kivu’da ise 75 gündür yeni doğrulanmış vakaya rastlanmadığı belirtildi.

Salgının kontrol altına alınabilmesi için temaslı kişilerin takibinin sürdüğü, temaslı takip oranının yüzde 82,7 seviyesine ulaştığı bildirildi.

Sağlık yetkilileri, mayıs ayında ortaya çıkan Bundibugyo Ebola varyantına karşı henüz onaylanmış bir tedavi veya aşının bulunmadığını belirtiyor.

Ebola virüsü, kanamalı ateşe yol açan ve yüksek ölüm oranına sahip bir hastalığa neden oluyor. Virüs ilk kez 1976’da Sudan’ın Nzara ve KDC’nin Yambuku kentlerinde eş zamanlı salgınlarla tespit edildi. KDC’deki ilk salgının Ebola Nehri yakınlarında ortaya çıkması nedeniyle hastalığa bu nehrin adı verildi.

Ebola, 2013’ün sonunda Batı Afrika’da yeniden geniş çaplı bir salgına yol açmıştı. Gine, Liberya ve Sierra Leone’de 2014-2017 yılları arasında yaşanan salgında yaklaşık 30 bin kişiye virüs bulaşmış, 11 binden fazla kişi hayatını kaybetmişti.

KDC’nin doğusundaki Ituri eyaletinde 246 şüpheli vaka ve 65 ölümün ardından 15 Mayıs’ta ülkede yeni Ebola salgını ilan edilmişti.

Son veriler, KDC’de sağlık sisteminin salgının yayılmasını önleme konusunda ağır bir yükle karşı karşıya olduğunu ortaya koyuyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Galatasaray Lisesi'ne geçişte sınav zorunluluğu getirildi
content:
Fotoğraf: Nicoleon/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0

Galatasaray Üniversitesi'ne bağlı Galatasaray Lisesi, Ortaokulu ve İlkokulu Yönetmeliğinde Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB) tarafından değişikliğe gidildiği duyuruldu.

Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan yeni düzenlemeye göre, Galatasaray Ortaokulunu bitiren öğrencilerin liseye geçişi artık merkezi sınav sonucuna bağlandı. Buna göre MEB tarafında yapılan LGS sınavında ilk yüzde 4'lük dilime giremeyen öğrenciler Galatasaray Lisesine kayıt olamayacak. LGS'de ilk yüzde 4'lük dilime giren öğrenciler okul tarafından gerçekleştirilen Fransızca ve Türkçe yeterlilik sınavlarına da girecek. Öğrencilerin bu sınavlardan da en az 70 puan alması gerekiyor. Dil sınavından yeterlilik alamayanlar ise Fransızca hazırlık sınıfına alınacak.

Öte yandan bu düzenlemenin önümüzdeki 2026-2027 eğitim öğretim yılından önce ilkokul birinci sınıfa kaydolan öğrenciler için uygulanmayacağı ifade etti. Bu uygulamayla birlikte öğrenciliklerine devam edenlerin hakları koruma altında olacak.

title: Çiftçi-Sen: Kuru üzüm fiyatı en az 151,50 TL olmalı
content:
Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

Ege Bölgesinde üzüm üreticileri tarladaki ürünün satış fiyatı ve yüksek üretim maliyetleri nedeniyle derin bir krizle karşı karşıya. Duruma dikkat çeken Çiftçiler Sendikası (Çiftçi-Sen) yaptığı açıklama yüksek enflasyon ve kontrolsüz tarım girdilerinin bağcılığı sürdürülemez bir noktaya getirdiğini vurguladı.

Üretim alanlarında artan madencilik faaliyetleri ve enerji projelerinin ortama salınan asit, gaz ve toz emisyonları nedeniyle üzüm bağlarına doğrudan zarar verdiğini belirten Çiftçi-Sen çiftçilerin bağlarını petrol türevi naylon örtülerle kapatmak zorunda kalmasının ekstra masraf kalemlerine sebep olduğunu ifade etti.

Çiftçi-Sen girdi maliyetleri 3-4 kat artarken üzüm alım fiyatlarının geriye gittiğine dikkat çekti. Yapılan açıklamada, 2024 yılında litresi 41–44 TL bandında seyreden, 2025’te 45–53 TL’ye çıkan mazot fiyatı, 2026 yılına 55 TL ile başlayıp kısa sürede yüzde 50 artışla 83 TL’ye yükseldiği dile getirildi. Buna karşılık geçen yıl 16–18 TL/kg bandında olan sumalık yaş üzüm alım fiyatı bu sezon 11 TL/kg seviyesinden açıldığı ifade edildi.

Türkiye’nin dünya kuru üzüm ihracatının %30-35’ini karşılamasına rağmen alım fiyatlarının küresel şirketler tarafından belirlendiğini ve devletin üreticiyi şirketlerin insafına bıraktığını vurgulayan Çifti-Sen, ayrıca, denetimsizlik nedeniyle binlerce çiftçiyi mağdur eden dolandırıcı şirketlere karşı caydırıcı cezai yaptırımların uygulanmadığına dikkat çekti.

Çiftçi-Sen şaraplık üzüm üreten çiftçilerin ürünlerini kendi olanaklarıyla işleyip katma değerli ürün olarak satması katı mevzuat ve ağır vergi şartlarıyla engellediğini ifade etti. Tekel’in özelleştirilmesi sonrasında devreden çıkan kamusal mekanizma, üreticiyi bir avuç şarap fabrikasının fiyat politikasına mahkûm ederken, devletin tüketim aşamasındaki yüksek dolaylı vergileri tahsil etmekle yetindiği eleştirisi yapıldı.

Sendika tarafından yapılan açıklamada üeticinin üretime devam edebilmesi ve insanca yaşayabilmesi için 93,00 TL/kg yalın maliyetin üzerine %25 kâr Payı ve %30 insanca yaşam payı eklenerek 2026 yılı çekirdeksiz kuru üzüm referans taban fiyatının en az 151,50 TL/kg olması gerektiği belirtildi.

Çiftçi-Sen şu talepleri dile getirdi:

Gücünü uluslararası sözleşmelerden ve Anayasa’dan alan çiftçilerin sendikal örgütlenmeleri fiyat belirlemelerinde sürece dahil edilmelidir.

TARİŞ, üretimden pazarlamaya kadar olan zincirin her halkasında, yönetim organlarında, üreticilerin söz ve karar sahibi olacağı şekilde yeniden yapılandırılmalı, kuru üzüm alımında devreye sokulmalıdır.

Kuru üzüm fiyatlarında maliyet, kar payı ve insanca yaşam payı gözetilerek sendikamızın referans fiyatları üzerinden TARİŞ tarafından destekleme alımı yapılmalı, hükümet bu konuda destek vermelidir.

Şaraplık üzüm üreten üreticilerin üzümlerini işleyip satabilecekleri yasal düzenlemeler yapılmalı ve ürünlerini işleyerek satmaları konusunda teşvikler verilmelidir.

İklimi ve üretimi olumsuz etkileyen enerji ve madencilik faaliyetlerine tarımsal alanlarda izin verilmemeli, faaliyette olanlar da kapatılmalıdır.

Çiftçileri dolandıran şirket veya kişileri ticaretten men etme, deşifre etme ve caydırıcı cezalar verme konusunda yasal düzenlemeler yapılmalıdır.

Tarım Sigortaları Yasası yeniden düzenlenmelidir.

Kamu agroekolojik üretime yönelen üreticilere teşvikler vermelidir.

author: Leandro Barbosa
title: “Onde tem malária, tem garimpo”: cinta larga aguardam decisão do STF sobre mineração
content:
Os indígenas Cinta Larga estão divididos sobre a regulamentação da mineração em suas terras, e o tema pode ter uma decisão do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que julga nesta quinta-feira, 13, o Mandado de Injunção 7.516, que cobra a regulamentação da mineração no território a partir de uma demanda apresentada por uma associação do povo Cinta Larga (Patjamaaj). O pedido da associação a Dino vai na direção contrária ao posicionamento de outras organizações indígenas, como a Articulação dos Povos Indígenas do Brasil (Apib).


Nas vésperas do julgamento, um relatório do Distrito Sanitário Especial Indígena (DSEI) Vilhena, obtido com exclusividade pela

Agência


Pública

, revela o impacto da exploração mineral no território localizado entre Rondônia e Mato Grosso.


O documento registra 133 casos de malária em 2026, segundo o Sistema de Informação da Atenção à Saúde Indígena (Siasi) e mostra que diabetes e hipertensão cresceram dezenas de vezes desde 2000. No período, os casos de diabetes entre os Cinta Larga saltaram de 2 para 107 (alta de 5.250%), enquanto os registros de hipertensão passaram de 4 para 131(alta de 3.175%). A escalada incide sobre uma população de mais 1600 indígenas, distribuídos em 59 aldeias nas Terras Indígenas Roosevelt, Parque do Aripuanã e Serra Morena e Aripuanã.


Os registros aparecem tanto em aldeias quanto em áreas identificadas como garimpos, entre elas Ouro Preto, Laje Roosevelt, Flor do Prado e Madalena. Para o DSEI Vilhena, a sobreposição entre áreas de transmissão e localidades submetidas à atividade garimpeira é um achado epidemiologicamente relevante.


Vinculado à Secretaria de Saúde Indígena (Sesai), do Ministério da Saúde, o DSEI Vilhena é responsável pela atenção à saúde indígena na região e acompanha os Cinta Larga. Procurado pela

Pública

, o Ministério da Saúde informou que não comentaria os dados apresentados no relatório.


O território dos Cinta Larga, que totaliza 2,7 milhões de hectares na divisa do Mato Grosso com Roraima, fica em uma das maiores jazidas do mundo de kimberlito — rocha que forma diamantes


Cinta Larga: “Onde tem malária, a gente sabe que tem garimpo”


Uma indígena Cinta Larga, ouvida pela reportagem sob condição de anonimato, afirma que a repetição de casos de malária já pode ser observada entre crianças e adolescentes. “Já encontrei a situação de um adolescente de 14 anos que passou por vários e vários tratamentos para malária. Faz o tratamento, toma o remédio, cura a malária, aí vai novamente para a região onde estão ocorrendo os casos e adquire a doença novamente. E isso vai danificando o corpo, causando outras problemáticas”, relata. “Onde tem malária, a gente sabe que tem garimpo. Você chega no território e já está cheio de casos. Então, já não se consegue trabalhar com a prevenção, apenas com o tratamento da doença”, explica.


Somente no primeiro trimestre de 2026, um surto na Terra Indígena Roosevelt registrou 62 casos confirmados, incluindo crianças e gestantes. O relatório ajuda a explicar por que a doença se torna persistente em áreas de exploração mineral. O DSEI classifica a malária como o achado epidemiológico de “maior relevância” para compreender a relação entre o território e a saúde dos Cinta Larga.


O documento ressalta que os dados disponíveis não permitem estabelecer uma relação causal entre cada caso individual de malária e a atividade garimpeira. Mas considera que a concentração territorial da doença, associada às alterações ambientais e à mobilidade populacional características do garimpo, sustenta a necessidade de tratar a atividade como um importante elemento do contexto de risco e de vulnerabilidade para a transmissão.


Dados disponíveis não permitem estabelecer uma relação causal entre cada caso individual de malária e a atividade garimpeira.


Cinta Larga: aumento da diabetes


A malária representa apenas uma parte de uma transformação mais ampla no perfil de saúde dos Cinta Larga. Em 2000, havia dois registros de diabetes e quatro de hipertensão. Em 2025, eram respectivamente 86 e 111. Na atualização de 2026, os números voltaram a subir: são 107 indígenas registrados com diabetes e 131 com hipertensão.


Hoje, o número de pacientes com hipertensão corresponde a pouco mais de 8% dos 1.606 Cinta Larga registrados pelo DSEI. Os pacientes com diabetes representam cerca de 6,7% dessa população. Os percentuais não representam necessariamente a prevalência epidemiológica, pois se referem aos registros de pacientes acompanhados …

title: Fetî Yildizê MHPyî: Demîrtaş di çarçoveya qanûnê de ye
content:
Alîkarê Serokê Giştî yê MHPyê Fetî Yildiz ji weşana zindî ya Haberturkê re peyamek şand û diyar kir ku Selahattîn Demîrtaş di çarçoveya yasaya nû de ye.


"Qanûna Çarçoveyê" ji aliyê Lijneya Giştî ya Parlamentoyê ve hat pejirandin.


Piştî qebûlkirina yasayê, li ser mijara “Gelo Hevserokê berê yê HDPyê Selahattîn Demîrtaş dê ji vê yasayê sûdê wergire yan na?” daxuyaniyên cuda hatin dayîn.


Daxuyaniya parêzerê Demîrtaş


Mahsunî Karamanê parêzerê Selahattîn Demîrtaş, berê li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî bal kişandibû ser vê mijarê û gotibû:


“Demirtaş û hevalên wî tenê ji ber xala 302yan a Qanûna Cezê a Tirkan (TCK) girtî ne ku ew xal di nav çarçoveya qanûnê de ye. Dema ku ev biryar bikeve meriyetê, ji bo berdana wan ji aliyê hiqûqî ve ti guman nîne.”


Fetî Yildiz name şand


Rojnameger Alîşer Delek di bernameyeke televîzyona Haberturkê de li ser mijarê got:


“Kekê wî Nurettîn Demîrtaşê ku di nav kadroyên çiyê de ye dê vegere lê rewşa Selahattîn Demîrtaş ne zelal e.”


Rojnameger Delek piştî vê nirxandina xwe eşkere kir ku Alîkarê Serokê Giştî yê MHPyê Fetî Yildiz ji wî re peyamek şandiye.


Delek li ser peyama ku ji Fetî Yildiz hatiye wiha axivî:


“Min di weşanê de behsa rewşa Demîrtaş kir. Min got 'Nurettîn Demirtaşê birayê wî dê vegere lê rewşa Selahattîn Demîrtaş ne diyar e.' Birêz Fetî Yildiz, ji weşana Haberturkê re notek şand û got, "Selahattîn Demîrtaş di çarçoveya yasayê de ye.'”

title: Remzi Kartal: This process cannot develop without Abdullah Öcalan and the state knows it
content:
The “Bill on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” prepared as part of the “Democratic Society and Peace Process” with the aim of ending the armed struggle and establishing its legal framework, was submitted to the Turkish Parliament on August 5. The 12-article bill covers a range of issues, from the legal status of those laying down their arms to oversight mechanisms, while sparking debate because it does not address the political and constitutional dimensions of the Kurdish issue. The article was approved by parliament on Tuesday night.


Speaking to ANF about the new situation and the debates surrounding it, KONGRA GEL co-chair Remzi Kartal said they did not view the framework law as a final regulation that would solve the issue on its own, but rather as the legal beginning of a process aimed at moving the struggle onto a political and democratic footing after decades of conflict.


Pointing to significant shortcomings in terms of the scope and language of the law, Kartal said that the return of people from the mountains and Europe, their legal status, military service, restrictions on political activities and implementation mechanisms would all have to be addressed in the coming stages.


Emphasizing that new legal regulations as well as issues of dialogue and negotiation would come onto the agenda in the later stages of the process, Kartal also drew attention to Abdullah Öcalan’s practical coordinating role.


Kartal said that the fact that Öcalan does not have an explicitly defined status in the law does not mean he will not play a role in the process. In particular, he stated that returns to Turkey from the mountains and Europe could not take place without Öcalan’s coordination and calls. He added that, if the process advances, ensuring Öcalan’s conditions for free life and work would also become part of the legal agenda in subsequent stages.


Remzi Kartal said the significance of the framework law could only be understood by considering the circumstances in which it emerged together with the process underway. Recalling the policies of conflict, denial and destruction experienced over the past century, Kartal said that conditions were being created for dialogue and the struggle over the Kurdish issue to move from a military conflict environment to a political-democratic ground. He described the law’s place within this process as follows: “We need to assess the importance of this law by taking into account the circumstances in which it emerged and the process. In other words, after a century of conflict, denial and destruction, this is a process in which conditions are being created for dialogue and the struggle over the Kurdish issue to move from a military conflict environment to a political-democratic ground. That is the aim. Therefore, the law is not everything; it simply opens a door in relation to this process. It would not be right to expect too much from the law beyond that.


The Kurdish issue will not be resolved by this law. This law is simply a step toward clearing the way for democratic political struggle. If we approach the matter on this basis, the law that has now been adopted does not fully meet our expectations or provide an adequate response to the need for a comprehensive struggle for democratization. But when considered as a door, an entry point and a step that will clear the way for democratic political struggle, it is important."


Kartal added: “The law’s wording, language and many of its aspects can be criticized because of their shortcomings and inadequacies. It should have been more inclusive. In other words, restrictions have been imposed concerning arrivals both from the mountains and from Europe, and there are serious shortcomings in this regard. Likewise, linguistic elements such as the use of the word ‘terror’ constitute a shortcoming in terms of a political-democratic sphere in which ideas should be expressed freely.


Taken as a whole, although it does not provide a complete response to our expectations, we can say that, in essence, it is a historic step that helps open the way for dialogue and a democratic basis for the development of this strategic process.”


Kartal underlined that the law had been presented as a measure adopted for the transition period, but emphasized that it could not be regarded merely as a technical transitional arrangement. He stressed the need for a framework that would also encompass the participation in social life of those …

title: [Appel] Non au permis de tuer !
content:
Appel unitaire pour une grande marche contre la loi instaurant la présomption de légitime défense pour les policiers. Rendez-vous le 19 septembre


SAVE

, avec le Comité Justice pour Adama, uni aux familles de victimes de violences et de crimes policiers, syndicats de la justice, associations de défense des droits humains et organisations syndicales, appelle à une grande marche nationale unitaire le 19 septembre 2026 contre la loi instaurant une présomption de légitime défense pour les forces de l'ordre.


Derrière son jargon juridique, cette loi n'est rien d'autre qu'un permis de tuer en toute impunité.


Elle légitime une violence qui cible d'abord des vies considérées comme sacrifiables.


Mais une loi qui autorise la police à tirer sans rendre de comptes ne s'arrête jamais à sa première cible. Aujourd'hui les quartiers populaires, demain les manifestant-es, les grévistes et toutes celles et ceux qui défendent leurs droits et leurs libertés.


Tant que son parcours législatif n'est pas achevé, nous pouvons encore l'arrêter. Le 19 septembre, partout en France, unissons-nous et faisons de cette journée une mobilisation massive.


C'est maintenant qu'il faut agir.

title: Je t'écoute. Tu m'écoutes
content:
Compte rendu de la commission mandatée par la commission Bloquons Tout Paris du lundi 20 juillet 2026


Règlement des prises de parole dans la commission

BLOQUONS


TOUT


Tu me laisses parler. Je t'ai écouté. Donc tu me laises parler.

TU


ME


LAISSES


PARLER

 . Je t'ai écouté.

DONC


TU


ME


LAISSES


PARLER


(etc etc)


Motion concernant ce réglement de prise de paroles


Tu m'écoutes, je t'écoute et tu me laisses parler sont des phrases de domination permettant de cadrer et d'enfermer la problématique de la discussion dans un seul sujet, celui défini par celui qui a pris la parole et qui entend contrôler par tous les moyens la finalité de sa prise de parole.


L'écoute n'est pas le respect, le droit, le devoir et le mérite. L'écoute n'est pas retour sur investissement. Notre écoute n'est pas celle d'Emmanuel Macron, de Marine Le Pen, de Jean Luc Mélenchon, des représentants du Syndicat Unitaire et Démocratique (

SUD

), du Nouveau Parti Anticapitaliste (

NPA

), du parlement, du directeur du personnel, de l'école et des associations.

 L'écoute est l'expérimentation et le partage de nos souffrances qui deviendront peut-être des actes. Désormais nos réunions, l'éducation populaire, les coordinations, les ateliers de travail de réflexion, les congrès et nos manifestations deviendront des ripostes et du désordre proclamé comme désordre par les professionnels de l'écoute.


Notre écoute est fondée sur le désir, elle n'est pas fondée sur l'échange commercial et elle deviendra une énergie collective incontrôlable, puisque dénuée du sens unique, de la visibilité, du plan comptable et de l'ouverture aux autres.


Qui aurait pu prévoir que l'absence d'écoute suivie d'actes chers à Victor Hugo et d'autres humanistes à l'écoute deviendraient des drones et la destruction des chars et de la barrière de sécurité

 

?


Qui se souviendra des trois millions de manifestants défilant contre la réforme des retraites avec comme mot d'ordre parfaitement justifié le mot d'ordre de la lutte contre la réforme des retraites

 

?


Désormais, nous tournerons en rond devant les supermarchés le dimanche, le samedi ou le vendredi soir après 19 heures 41, sans porte-paroles, sans but, sans votre raison et sans votre encadrement destiné à encadrer vos crises de panique. La répétition est la subversion de leurs victoires et de leur ordre ordonné par l'écoute tolérante.

author: Jamil Jonna
title: John Bellamy Foster’s “Breaking the Bonds of Fate”
content:
In the Public Eye


GPEnewsdocs, with Lynn Fries:


In the 1st segment of an interview series on ecology and materialism conducted by journalist Lynn Fries, John Bellamy Foster explains how Marx, who was not a natural scientist learned from chemists, physicists, biologists and the ancient Greek philosopher Epicurus. Marx then garnered a unique theoretical approach that identifies the causes of the societal and ecological crises we face today. In Part 2, Foster debunks the misconception that socialism and materialism had no role in the development of ecological analysis. His research shows that socialist transformation involves the transformation of human relations with nature, and that the modern ecological movement grew out of Marx’s analysis of the dialectics of society and nature. And there again, the Epicurean strand carries right through. In the 3rd segment, Foster concludes that across different societies starting from ancient China, the Hellenistic world and India, there is a parallelism of class struggles. They involve notions of self-consciousness through production in relation with nature, human freedom, solidarity and substantive equality. Common to them is a praxis that combines Epicurus’s philosophy of enough and reciprocity with Marx’s emphasis on production and transformation. Says Foster in Part 1:

“….Epicurus for Marx was a plus because he was very critical of religion or teleology – the notion that the gods or God determined things on earth. He rejected that without rejecting religion completely. And he emphasized that the basis of human life was community, friendship; building a society based on friendship. He was the first to bring women into philosophy – allowing them to emerge as major philosophers within the Epicurean school – and also slaves. He couldn’t do anything about slavery itself, but he brought slaves into Epicurean philosophy. They were given a high status. The whole society was organized around a garden. And emphasized sustainable living, and very ecological in orientation. Epicurus criticized those who thought that, “enough was too little”. The idea is that everyone needs enough but no one needs more than that….”


Read more here

 and

watch here

.


Emancipations with Daniel Tutt


In late May, Helena Sheehan, Katarina Kolozova, Thomas Nail joined John Bellamy Foster in discussing his latest book,

Breaking the Bonds of Fate: Epicurus and Marx

, in a symposium hosted by Daniel Tutt.

We encourage you to support

Emancipations with Daniel Tutt

, a series of public discussions on seminal works in the history of Marxist thought and philosophy.

Watch below….


The Critical Theory Workshop


The Critical Theory Workshop was first to launch John Bellamy Foster’s excellent new work. Speakers alongside Foster included Boris Hennig and Paul Schafer, with Jennifer Ponce de León of The Critical Theory Workshop serving as the moderator: https://www.youtube.com/live/1PrDLsHiKkk


REVIEWS


Socialism and Democracy,

 by Mat Callahan


“The title of John Bellamy Foster’s latest book,

Breaking the Bonds of Fate

, derives from Lucretius’s famed De Rerum Natura, usually translated as On the Nature of Things. Lucretius wrote:

“Again, if all movement is always interconnected, the new arising from the old in a determinate order – if the atoms never swerve so as to originate some new movement that will break the bonds of fate, the everlasting sequence of cause and effect – what is the source of the free [will] … .” ([On the Nature of Things,] Book II, 251ff)

This exact quotation, moreover, was one made by Karl Marx in his Epicurean Notebooks, compiled in preparation for his doctoral thesis: “The Difference Between the Democritean and Epicurean Philosophy of Nature” of 1841. From this point of departure, Foster initiates the reappraisal of two thousand years of philosophical controversy…


…

Breaking the Bonds of Fate

is a major contribution to our understanding of the history of philosophy. Furthermore, it demonstrates the continued relevance of philosophy today. Especially at a time like ours, when social disintegration, irrationalism and reaction are rampant, the praxis and enduring influence of Epicurus and the Garden is an inspiration. By reaffirming basic principles of materialism, dialectics, and the work of Marx and Engels, Foster has provided persuasive arguments for their propagation. It is to be hoped that this wonderful book will be read and discussed by many. We will be better …

title: Voces indígenas sobre la ley que pone en peligro su territorio
content:
En los días previos a tratarse en el Senado Nacional la Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, hubo numerosas manifestaciones en contra de esa ley a lo largo y ancho del país, y al día siguiente, el jueves 6, tuvieron lugar innumerables actos y movilizaciones en donde se expresó con mucho fervor ese rechazo.  Incluso en la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, en la movilización en la Plaza Congreso, convocada por organizaciones sociales, políticas y de Derechos Humanos, se hicieron presentes, además de organizaciones indígenas locales, referentes de diversos pueblos y comunidades originarios de distintos lugares del país.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Espacio-Buen-Vivir-Kay-Pacha.mp3


Descargar audio


Efectivamente, además del resultado en el Senado, en donde el artículo referido a la ley del fuego también quedó afuera, así como anteriormente se había bajado la de extranjerización de la tierra, estas convocatorias dieron cuenta que sólo movilizándose y haciendo oír su voz, el pueblo puede conseguir importantes resultados.


De todos modos, todavía no se pueden  bajar los brazos porque ahora ese proyecto de ley pasará Diputados y queda todavía la ley  de  desalojos express en jurisdicción federal, que pone en riesgo a las comunidades originarias; la ley de expropiaciones, que complica la resolución de conflictos territoriales y no menos peligroso es el nuevo Registro de Propiedad Inmueble, que no menciona a los pueblos originarios, ni garantiza la inscripción de la propiedad comunitaria indígena.


Por eso queremos compartirles parte de las voces indígenas que se levantaron en esta oportunidad y que representan a miles de voces que se alzan en defensa de su territorio.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 12 août
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 12 août se met en grève et voit voler les pavés, tente de les mettre "à hauteur d'un empire" comme dit le poète. Sans oublier quelques tonnes d'explosifs par-ci par-là, pour la forme.


1861 :

 Naissance à Verceil (dans la Piémont) de l'anarchiste italien Luigi Galleani, qui deviendra une figure très importante de la lutte anarchiste aux Etats-Unis, tant par ses écrits que par les séries d'actions directes que de nombreux anarchistes mènent à cette époque. Le journal qu'il contribue à créer,

Cronaca Sovversiva

, est à l'époque considéré par le président comme étant "le journal le plus dangereux édité sur le sol des Etats-Unis".


1888 :

 A Barcelone, création du syndicat UGT.


1893 :

 Premier numéro du journal anarchiste

L'insurgé

 à Lyon.


1919 :

 Au Costa Rica, le dictateur Pelico Tinoco s'enfuit du pays avec plus de 100.000 dollars sur à une grève générale déclenchée par l'assassinat d'un professeur


1921 :

 A Almería, naissance d'Abel Paz (de son vrai nom Diego Camacho Escamez), anarcho-syndicaliste et historien, qui participa à la guerre civile.


1962 :

 En Espagne, le Mouvement Libertaire Espagnol et le groupe Défense Intérieure, lié aux résistant-e-s anarchistes à la dictature franquiste fait sauter une bombe dans la Basilique de Valle de los Caídos contre les liens entre l'Opus Dei et la dictature.


1969 :

 A Derry, en Irlande du Nord, c'est le début de la Bataille du Bogside entre la population et les membres loyalistes de l'armée britannique : trois jours d'émeutes presques ininterrompues qui font neuf morts et plus de 750 blessé-e-s (dont 150 par balles).


1977 :

 A Potenza, une attaque à l'explosif des NAP (Nuclei Armati Proletari) contre une caserne de carabinieri est abandonnée au dernier moment du fait de l'arrivée inopinée d'une patrouille. Tout le matériel, y compris une voiture volée, est laissé sur place.


1992 :

 La police métropolitaine de Londres découvre douze tonnes d'explosifs artisanaux lorsqu'elle saisit trois vans. Ceux-ci auraient été confectionnés par l'IRA.


1995 :

 En Irlande du Nord, la ville de Derry s'enflamme de nouveau et connait une journée d'émeutes.


2016 :

 A Gênes, des répétiteurs de télévision

sont incendiés

 en soutien aux prisonniers anarchistes et aux révolutionnaires en cavale.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 12 août.

author: Susan Price
title: ‘Reclaiming History’ preserves the legacy of Indonesia’s pro-democracy movement for new generations
content:
An exhibition and seminar titled Reclaiming History: Reflection on the past and future of progressive movements in post-Suharto Indonesia will take place at Taman Ismail Marzuki — an arts, cultural and science centre in Indonesia’s capital Jakarta — on August 29. Register here to attend.

Green Left has made available some of its photographs and posters from the Australian solidarity campaigns with the movement against the Suharto dictatorship for this important event. GL’s Peter Boyle spoke to exhibition organiser Esty Pratiwi Lubarman.

Please tell our readers a bit about the groups organising this event?

This event is organised by the Institute of Indonesian Socialist History (Lembaga Sejarah Sosialis Indonesia, LSSI) in collaboration with the Indonesian People’s History Foundation (Yayasan Sejarah Rakyat Indonesia, YSRI) and supported by the Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung.

LSSI is an initiative established to uncover, document and preserve the historical legacy and critical literature of the Indonesian left movement that was systematically suppressed during the Suharto “New Order” dictatorship.

By collecting both official and unofficial archives — such as newspapers, journals, organisational documents, photographs and audio-visual recordings — LSSI is committed to providing a space for political education and critical reflection for working people, current movements and young people to ensure that this history of resistance is not forgotten.

What will be on display and who will be the speakers in the seminar?

The event is structured around two main discussion formats — a public seminar and a webinar — alongside an archival exhibition. For the onsite public seminar, the speakers include representatives from socialist youth organisations, 1998 uprising activists and historians. The webinar will feature ’98 activists, historians and representatives from LSSI.

Running alongside these discussions, the archival exhibition, titled Techne of Movement: Capturing the movement against authoritarianism, beyond spontaneity, will display a range of historical attributes and artifacts from the Reformasi [democratic reform] era.

Visitors will be able to see protest banners, People’s Democratic Party election t-shirts, documentary photos, audio-visual recordings, meeting minutes and underground propaganda material.

The exhibition concept will feature three periods of the 1998 Reformasi.

The first is the movement-building period (the 1980s to 1996), which highlights the development of the progressive movement at the peak of the New Order repression, when various forms of the regime’s domination were carried out to restrict every form of resistance.

The second is the period of the 1998 Reformasi momentum — tracing the breaking point of the 1997–98 economic crisis, which culminated in a wave of mass resistance and the collapse of the New Order regime. This period will showcase the various elements of the progressive movement that converged at a single historical juncture.

The third is the post-Reformasi period, which will show how the dynamics of the progressive movement unfolded once the space for democratisation opened up, along with the fragmentation the movement had to confront.

The exhibition features secured glass display cases, LED screens showing looping archival footage and a dedicated platform (“Zone of Movement Organisation Stands”) where contemporary left-wing youth organisations can showcase their ideas, literature and current movement techniques.

What is the objective of this event and why is it important that it is taking place now?

The main objective of this event is to draw concrete lessons from the struggle against the New Order military regime, highlight the contributions of the Indonesian left and pro-democracy movements in opening up democratic spaces and create a space for critical reflection on the trajectory of progressive movements today. Additionally, it aims to provide a platform for youth organisations to publicise their perspectives and current struggles.

This event now is crucial to re-establish and uphold the tradition of struggle against the New Order military regime. This has become especially urgent in light of the current political context, where several former ’98 activists have chosen to co-opt with and support the Prabowo-Gibran regime. This dynamic demonstrates that the project of de-politicisation and historical distortion has not ended.

This serves not only to preserve collective …

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Hundreds protest Tasmania’s renewed fish farming licenses
content:
Hundreds protest Tasmania’s renewed fish farming licenses


Isaac Nellist


Wed, 12/08/2026 - 13:18


Philip Bohle

,

Nipaluna/Hobart


August 12, 2026

,


Issue 1460

,


News


A Fish Farms Out of Our Bays snap rally on August 11 brought together several hundred opponents of the Environmental Protection Authority’s recent decision to renew licences for 16 salmon farms on the Tasman Peninsula for up to two years.


See also


Dirty salmon and the corporate takeover of Tasmania’s waters


Tasmanian election results show anger at business as usual


The event was supported by the Bob Brown Foundation, the Tasmanian Greens and various community groups, including the Cremorne Ocean Dippers and Neighbours of Fish Farming.


Speakers included Alistair Allan, Bob Brown Foundation; Trish Baily, vice president of the Tasmanian Alliance of Marine Protection; independent MP Peter George; and Tasmanian Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff.


Salmon farms are 'killing our coast'. Photo: Philip Bohle


Serious warnings from scientific experts, and the Parliament’s Fin Fish Inquiry, have prompted widespread public opposition to salmon farming in Tasmania.


An online repository,

salmonbusters.org

, helps Tasmanians track the extent and impact of salmon farming. More than 60 leases are run by three subsidiaries of large foreign-owned multinationals. They consist of hundreds of pens, holding more than 100,000 tonnes of salmon.


These farms use 20 per cent of Tasmania’s fresh water and extensive treat disease in farmed salmon with more than 31.4 tones of antibiotics. They release more than 4,800 tonnes of nitrogen pollution per year.


Photo: Philip Bohle


Tasmanian Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff addresses the protest. Photo: Philip Bohle

title: Vale ‘Bolshi Bob’ — active to the end
content:
A friend and comrade Robert (Bob) Hart, affectionately known as “Bolshi Bob”, passed away recently, having just turned 80.

Bob’s life principles were based on solidarity, opposition to oppression and exploitation and support for working-class struggles.

Bob was actively involved in the anti-Vietnam War movement. Witnessing the horrendous war against Vietnam led him to oppose the capitalist system that caused wars like the US onslaught on the Vietnamese people.

He joined the Socialist Workers Party in the early 1970s and, in 2019, the Socialist Alliance.

Bob worked in the Commonwealth Employment Service and was a lifelong unionist. He was active in the Administrative and Clerical Officers’ Association, which covered public servants at the time and that later merged into the Commonwealth Public Service Union.

Bob was very active until the end, attending protests, political meetings and helping promote issues. He took part in the Unite Against Racism rally in Broadmeadows on July 5.

He was a big supporter of the movement for justice in Palestine and against the genocide in Gaza. Much earlier, Bob had studied in Italy, where he was introduced to the Palestinian struggle.

Bob was a film buff with a big collection of movies. He would get an annual pass to the Melbourne International Film Festival.

Above all, Bob was motivated by his love for humanity and hatred for capitalism that operates on the basis of destroying humanity.

Bob, who was often seen riding his electric bike around, will be deeply missed.
